"We know what happened after. Kuvida Nebula became a dead zone after the core went out of control. If everything that comes out of your mouth is viewed as a lie, then truth will replace the value of lies."
The Jokeless Beast can't take these jokes any longer and finally retaliates. Its stomach ulcer stirs up colossal waves and throws you and the ship into outer space.
"What an unfunny joke," the Fool laughs.

You are stopped by an IPC vending machine in the ruins of the Kingdom of Banditry. It does not have eyes, but you are certain that this vending machine is looking at you with a lonely, miserable, and piteous gaze right at this very moment.

As the only salesperson in the Talia region, it ranks at the very bottom of the sales department's charts because of its negative sales volume all year. There is only one reason for this: The customers here never pay when they buy anything.

"Please buy something. If I don't up my performance, I'll be fired from the IPC. I have a smart refrigerator and a robot vacuum to feed at home." It sounds so upset that you almost suspect there's a real person hiding in the vending machine.
"Thank you. You have a good heart." This is how you find out for the first time that a vending machine has the ability to touch its head to the ground.
"Don't worry. The quality of authentic IPC products is assured." You open the packaging and fall silent as you see that it has a shelf life of ten Amber Eras.
"Oh, you're like a second parent to me!" You decline the vending machine's praise, not wanting to add a strange vending machine to your family tree.
"You! You bullies!" Tears leak from the vending machine's battery box as it flails its mechanical limbs and lunges at you with a wail.

The dual-headed Intellitron detective in front of you is locked in self-debate. His logical circuits clash over conflicting conclusions, with the only resolution being a tie in an endless interstellar chess match.

The detective's golden circuit has considered countless possibilities, including a suspect slipping on a warp banana peel eight light-years away. His diamond circuit explores various motives, while the simulated suspect grapples with how to freeze mint-flavored machine oil.
"Hey, assistant, what are you waiting for? Go knock that fool out!" Both heads shout at you in unison.

"Well done! Based on my meticulous deduction, the suspect must have sought revenge on the victim for the purchase of expired magnetic toothpaste in the store." The detective resolutely projects an image of toothpaste with machine oil residue.

"I've listed <unbreak>12,222</unbreak> possibilities, but I'm inclined to believe that the tool in the crime is a customized holographic rose," says the detective as he confidently presents a paper report.
You stroll through a cold, deserted alley. The dazzling light dispels the shadows, revealing an incomplete painting resting quietly in a corner.
A monster lingers motionless on the paper, languishing in anticipation for someone to bring it back to life and grant it a tangible form through manifestation.
Despite not being a Punklordian hacker or a Mythus History Fictionologist, you feel confident that completing this painting with your artistic talent would be a walk in the park.
As the bright colors and lines fall, the one-eyed and one-legged monster is suddenly granted new life.
"Whew, fresh air at long last. Thanks." It shakes its body and makes its way out of the flat canvas, disappearing into the distant rainbow.
Upon opening your eyes again, you find yourself stranded on the edge of the data ocean alongside the wreckage of the ship.
As the bright colors and lines fall, the one-eyed and one-legged monster is suddenly granted new life.
"Whew, fresh air at long last. Thanks." It shakes its body and makes its way out of the flat canvas, disappearing into the distant rainbow.
You carefully wrap up the painting frame and sell it to a nearby monster collector with a decent reputation.

Paint falls haphazardly on the paper, sprinkling across the face of the sleeping monster like grime accumulated across many long years. It seems like it does not approve of your postcosmic style of abstract art.

No, no, no, you can't be the problem here. It's the paint. It's too low quality. Once you buy the highest-quality paint, you'll be able to paint this monster freehand, or even something like the Antimatter Legion.

As the most talented student in the studio, your art is avant-garde and worthy of praise from tens of thousands of patrons even at a mere Pier Point art exhibition. The reason this human you drew that so resembles a Shapeless creature could not fully manifest is just because of a difference in style.
Perhaps it's best to outsource this task of awakening the monster.
Viscous color flow across the paper, causing tears to fall from the monster's eye.
You're just rusty from not creating for so long. But it does not seem worth it to practice for the duration of a song for such a small painting.

You find yourself in a dilapidated royal city. Here, steel thorns wind around the sacred temple, while swarms of nanomachines depleted of their power source lie dormant, merely reflecting the radiant glow of the two suns.

You head toward the sacred temple. The colossal door is engraved with a portrait of the Wrath King, the sovereign of Planet Behrenger. Deceived by the Masked Fools, the Wrath King issued a decree that silenced all laughter within his kingdom.

The door has been blasted open by the Armed Archaeologists' explosives, but even in the wake of the King's demise, the entropy-limiting device within the Temple of Reticence persists in perpetual operation.
"Whoever has an audience with the King shall offer their wrath." You set your eyes on the inscription, grasping the significance it conveys.
It would be troublesome if an ancient interstellar zombie were to be unleashed in such an eerie place.
"Laughter is forbidden here." Waves of chanting reach your ears, prayers that send a shiver down your spine.
"Laughter is forbidden here." You defiantly burst into laughter, yet the sound dissipates into nothingness the moment it escapes your lips.

As the urge for destruction and wrath surge within your heart, you shatter the Curio in your hand. A faint tremor courses through the ground, and in the blink of an eye, the steel gate swings open before you.

You stand on the deck of the Invincible Voyager, watching the rippling waves on the surface of the water caused by the ship. The hacker sailors envelop the vessel in foam with aether editing, steering directly toward the dark side of the data ocean.

As you also press forward, massive data streams infiltrate the foam, a data storm that corrodes the vessel. A purple lionfish swims before you. Startled, you step back, promptly turning it back into code before its poisonous spines reach you.

In the dark web of Punklorde, this mere number combination of 0s and 1s is equivalent to an entire month's worth of equipment maintenance fees. You gaze into the unfathomable ocean, torn between the allure of vast opportunities and the peril of tempting fate.
Good morning, Punklorde! You shall soon embrace a new legend!
Keep persevering, young hacker. Your triumph will come one day!

A cluster of junk data collides with the ship at a rapid pace. The infiltrating code tears your vessel apart, assimilating the data it carries. Just before being dragged into the depths of darkness, you reluctantly activate the emergency eject button.
Upon opening your eyes again, you find yourself stranded on the edge of the data ocean alongside the wreckage of the ship.
There is always more code to be written as long as you still have your keyboard. As the most exceptional hacker in Punklorde, these trivial gains clearly won't sway your resolve.
You feel the weight of your own work in your hand, the two strings of code gleaming like gems within the bag.
Tenderly, you stroke the songbird's tail, within the feathers concealing the secret of a fabled hacker.
You disengage the network device within your brain, liberating yourself from the grip of deep data and returning to reality before slipping into unconsciousness.
You hasten the ship's pace, steering it back to the comparatively hospitable side of Punklorde before it succumbs to destruction.

You navigate into a cluster of deserted historical data. Here, you assume the role of the fleet vanguard of the Yellow Citrus Nebula, who pilots a consciousness-integrated airship that requires ten tentacles for control, deftly maneuvering through swarms of enemy floating cannons.

You breach the enemy's defensive encirclement. The disguised smart code attempts to hide itself within the ship's engine, only to be captured by you and brought back to the ship beyond the data. The sensation of returning to your human form is truly comforting.
Do you want to continue diving?

A bullet blasts by your ear. The graffiti data splatters everywhere, before being quickly programmed into explosives again. You narrowly escape the relentless pursuit of the assassin. Every frame of this timeless movie is etched into your memory.

In the upcoming scene, Traitor No. 5 will expose her Furnace Core to disperse the heat. You will take away her prosthetic eye, where her consciousness resides. Who would hide code within an old movie that sank into the ocean? You sense yourself gradually adapting to these unfamiliar waters.
Do you want to continue diving?
You sink into pink jelly, the taste of blue velvet still lingering on your palate. As you move your body, you find your limbs twisted like a jellyfish in a funhouse mirror and as crooked as macaroni.

You walk toward the periphery of the crystal unit. Following the Ternary Empire's unsuccessful conquest against the Binary Kingdom, fear permeates everyone's heart. When a binary intellitail songbird flies overhead, you whistle at it, compelling the code to obediently descend onto your fingertips.
Do you want to continue diving?

Legend has it that the fabled hacker known as Zero left behind a code string potent enough to shake the world, hidden in the depths of this ocean, yet no one has been able to uncover any traces of it.
The vessel of aether editing has reached its maximum capacity, yet your interest in seeking out his treasure has waned.
You have demonstrated both your prowess as a legend and your courage as a hacker.

Multiple currents converge here, giving rise to a paradise of chaos. You ride a mutant nosewalker, racing atop a Giant Sting. A masked mimicry cheetah walks upright and holds hands with an egret to engage in a dance.

Your limbs are extended by the space, and they are almost nibbled by the passing insects. Yet, a bird swoops in to carry them away, leaving behind a vial of transparent ink. When you open it, the illicit history of corporations in the Oasis Zone stains it in black.
Do you want to continue diving?

You sit cross-legged on the cushion as you lock eyes with the half-human half-snake shop owner. The excitement of the <unbreak>99</unbreak>th Staring Contest is reaching its peak. Even the water demon's two drinking buddies can't help but cover their mouths, for fear they would disturb this world-shattering showdown.
The lion-dog officer assigned to maintain order on the scene is nervously chowing down on dog food. Even the biker gang youth they cuffed under arrest is sweating over the contest.

"Give it up, young one. There are scant few in the Lafcadio — and fewer still in this Shopping Street — who can defeat me in this contest." The shop owner makes a threatening sound and her forked tongue almost touches your eyes.
"Hiss... Don't get too cocky now. There is always a stronger opponent," the shop owner laughs and flicks her forked tongue. "I am the weakest among the Four Unblinking Kings."
You're stubborn but you can feel your eyes becoming the desert of Planet Mio as they part ways with all water molecules.

You widen your eyes, trying to hurt your opponent's pupils with your gaze. Two pairs of eyes protrude in the air like the finest ornamental goldfish, almost popping out of their eye sockets to collide with each other like meteorites.

"Gah, I surrender." The shop owner painfully closes her eyes. In that moment, every human and monster cheers for your victory. As this year's champion, you get the chance to be the first to taste all limited-edition products in the candy store!

You enter a restaurant on Planet Adina. An old-fashioned sign in dazzling colors slowly rotates while informing patrons that dogs and Fools are not allowed entry. A tailless goldfish sits on a plate, its protruding fish eyes rotating as it chooses a taste experience that suits you.

"Gourmet cooking grants a sampling of life. A banquet of Xianzhou flavors is more worthy of your tongue's consideration than a showing of immersia." The goldfish makes a strange gurgling sound in its throat.
You catch the sweet smell of appetizers wafting in the private room, carrying three parts tender youth, three parts lingering spices, and four parts plant fiber that's still warm.

As you put the appetizer mixed with the past into your mouth, it soaks into your taste buds. The stimulation on the tip of your tongue overlaps with your senses. You are donned in standard armor as you take a step forward to embrace your calling as a Cloud Knight.
Fully vigilant, you raise your lance toward the demons and abominations sowing chaos in the world.
Fully patient, you maintain order and stability for the craftsmen on-site.

As you wake up from the sweet yet sour unrealizable dream, the second course has been served to your table. After whetting your appetite, you're supplemented with another life. You look at the eyes across the room, and it bundles you up in <unbreak>7,000</unbreak> seconds of memory, sinking your consciousness into the plate of sauce.

Sparks cover the sky and fall from it like rain. A starskiff intersects with a falling trajectory. As you're wrapped up in the delicious flavor on the tip of your tongue, the innumerable bulging goldfish eyes dotting the sky all smile at you.
You snap out of your daze and tightly grip the weapon in your hands. The next mission is very dangerous. As the squad leader of the Cloud Knights, you and your team lie in wait.
This sorcerer claims to be born with the power of gods and has never been touched by the plague. He could at least hide the elixir crucible on his back first.
The aurumaton before you is shouting some nonsense about unbreakable aurumatons and how they can fall in love too. Either way, it's best to subdue it first.
You swallow beautiful old memories. They have a spongy texture. The owner of the restaurant slaps the air with their fins. The final course is served to your table.

Among the seasoning of the small roasted fire serpent, unending layers of mountain ranges shield the soft and chewy texture beneath the crisp-fried surface like a protective screen. You want to refuse yet embrace it anyway. You transform into a breeze and drift across a cooling battlefield until you float among a sea of clouds.

After many years, the once-young man has become a famous Cloud Knight Lieutenant. Having stolen a moment of leisure, you down half a bowl of tea in the Exalting Sanctum. But the road ahead is long, and you still have unspent energy you yearn to put to use. You want to become a well-known hero on the Xianzhou!
You continue to surmount all obstacles in your way. As you look upon your opponents' swords, you know that this is also another life worth sampling.
You hoist your luggage onto your shoulder and walk into the port of the Xianzhou Yaoqing, where a new life for sampling awaits.
You are deep in a dense forest, an ancient temple entangled in vines looming before you.

A bouquet blooms from Mnestia's golden chrysalis, statues faded to alabaster white, poets surrounded by flitting butterflies, their bodies leaned against the edge of the stone steps, gently caressing the strings of their lyres.
"I have heard your sorrow, the ends of the westerly winds, tears intertwining like flowing streams. I sing a song of your love, upon Styxia's shores."
Their gazes fall from the ends of your hair, waiting for you to open your eyes once more, where only a few butterflies with iridescent wings are left.
"I have to chase after them." Your heart yells out in desire.
It extols the weave of a single golden thread, shedding its olden divine form, embarking on a journey in search of love.
Your hand passes through its wings, allowing the illusion to dissipate, leaving nary but a lingering murmur of the past upon your fingertips.
It mourns the fall of a Kremnoan king, a heroic and prideful warrior, caught and dragged beneath the wheels of an enemy chariot.
Your hand passes through its wings, allowing the illusion to dissipate, leaving nary but a lingering murmur of the past upon your fingertips.
It whispers of a reminiscent taste of honey brew, pursuing glorious heroes raising their goblets in merriment over swaying seas.
Your hand passes through its wings, allowing the illusion to dissipate, leaving nary but a lingering murmur of the past upon your fingertips.
It awaits a reunion that will never arrive, a time scintillating in gold, when poets encountered the Chrysalis of Gold's kin.
Your hand passes through its wings, allowing the illusion to dissipate, leaving nary but a lingering murmur of the past upon your fingertips.
Outside the city of Icatus, a warrior clad in heavy armor laughs heartily amidst a crowd. He brandishes the weapon in his hand, proclaiming himself kin of Georios.

"This here spear once pierced the chest of a sea monster, that servant of Phagousa with two hearts and nine heads. Were it not for the Titans' blessing upon me, I would never have escaped its maw alive."

Yet the chorus of praise fails to sate his vanity, and a murmur of doubts arises from the crowd. His eyes dart about restlessly, anxiously seeking a challenger to prove his strength. And then, your eyes meet.
The man winks at you, as if hinting to you to strike a private deal.
The man shakingly raises his spear, like a startled hedgehog.
You pay no heed to the man's request for reinforcements — who says that Georios' blessing can't be "strength in numbers"?
Your knee is hit by an arrow called wealth.
You find yourself amidst a finely wrought underground forge. Howling clangs of hammer on steel echo through the spiraling corridor.
A scholar of Aquila raises his blueprint in the air, comparing it to the half-finished device's form, at times pointing and gesturing at the areas that need improving.
"There should be a lens added here, folded inward, to correct the observational error on the Veil of Evernight."
"And then, I can prove that the entirety of Amphoreus is centered around Aquila, revolving in periodic motion!" The scholar mutters to himself over the thunderous clamor of the forge.
"How can this be? What's the point of my research, then?" The disheartened scholar tosses his refuted theories in a daze, raises his hammer, and brings it down heavily on the device.
The scholar scoffs at your mention of a "world beyond the sky," then casts your heretical self out of the workshop together with discarded steel scrap.
"Genius! Why don't I emulate the tyrants of old and create a skyship to see for myself?" You hope he stays far away from you when Aquila unleashes their wrath.
You stand at the heart of a celebration. The city square of Dolos bustles with excitement as the king prepares to unveil his invention with feigned mystery.

"This city once bore witness to two grand deceptions. The first time, even Zagreus, who managed to fool the other gods, was themself deceived. The second, when a shadowless thief brought forth puzzles to the former king. And now, I shall create the third miracle!" The king pulls back the black veil, revealing seven dice in seven colors spinning on its tray.

"I shall grant every citizen equal rights! As long as the fee is paid, everyone can participate in this game, which is beyond judgment. Seven dice, seven numbers. The more numbers you accurately guess, the better your rewards."
Chance and infinite possibilities — this is the king's invention. The citizens surge forth, eager in the notion that they may strike it rich overnight with the toss of a coin.
Clear your head, friend. Do not stake your future on the possibility of slim odds.
This city exudes an eerie, sticky sensation — once trapped within, you may not be able to escape its clutches.
You hear waves of booing around you. Their contempt for your retreat is palpable, yet envy the opportunity that Zagreus has bequeathed you.
You extract yourself from the fervent atmosphere, leaving Dolos as if fleeing from it, the relentless sounds of rolling dice behind you.
You leave the mad city of Dolos in a frenzied hurry, the relentless sounds of rolling dice echoing behind you.

The dice come to a halt, their numbers a far cry from your guess. You ignore the laments of failure — in this moment, only the jubilant cheers of winners can be heard. Hey, don't you want to try again?
The dice come to a halt, their numbers a far cry from your guess. You pat your own pockets — they have been gradually emptying out, a silent omen of your life's course.
As the dice come to a stop, your final gamble draws to a close.
The crowd isn't sighing at your failure. They are oblivious to your desolation, as their chants urge for the next round of Dolos dice.

The dice stop, and their numbers are identical to your guess. The success of positive reinforcement burgeons within you, gradually drowning out the warnings of risk. How about another roll? The voices of Dolos' onlookers are starting to melt together.
The dice stop, and their numbers are identical to your guess. Oh, the citizens lift you high, as if this slight chance also represents your status and destiny. How about another round?
As the dice come to a stop, your final gamble draws to a close.
The people's cheers reach you before your own joy does. They laud your great fortune, as if it were your very own virtue.
At the base of Epos' precipice, the maddened Titankin and monsters relentlessly pursue you from behind.
The collapsed bastion cuts the valley in half. From the statue's faded edges, they faintly reveal that it once belonged to a city that worshiped the Gate of Infinity.

You weave through the dilapidated ruins, attempting to navigate your way through shattered statues and altars, but a massive mirror on the stone wall blocks your way: "Those who enter must carry with them a thread of hope."
You have no time to ponder on the mirror's admonition. Muttering Janus' revered name under your breath, you dive into the mirror headfirst.
You tightly shut your eyes, as a thunderous crash echoes from the depths beneath your feet. You mutter Janus' name and press on.
You make the ascent cautiously, not daring to look down. An inexplicable sense of foreboding tells you that one wrong step, and you'll be devoured by the endless abyss below.
You can't tell how long you've walked, but a sturdy sensation finally meets your toes. Having survived the calamity, you let out a long sigh of relief and collapse to the ground.
The dampness of the grass, the fragrance of the earth... they all tell you that danger is far behind you. You stretch your arms, only for your hands to abruptly touch something cold.

"I hereby declare, you are guilty!" In the silent courtroom, the Intellitron judges' twenty-three fractals surround you, with a ruler symbolizing discipline stabbed into the digital network underground, like a flattened pipe organ.

"It has been reported that the defendant's life success index stands at an impressive <unbreak>99.9</unbreak>. In violation of regulations of Dirante Star's Second Codex, this has grievously overdrawn this system's collective success quota, constituting an egregious invasion upon the resources of others."

"Thus, this court hereby sentences you to undergo standardized failure therapy, until the balance between your success and failure index returns to the prescribed ratio." The judges raise their rulers and place them on your shoulders, as heavy electronic hums reverberate throughout the confined space.
You remorsefully bow your head, swallowing the bitter potion.
A future with occasional turmoil suits you far better than a smooth-sailing one.
But you firmly believe that no amount of failure will overshadow your radiance.
You're not going to accept the judge's twisted logic, and prepare to deliver true failure to it in response.

Thanatos' River of Souls soaks the ancient battlefield. You stand at the edge of the steps, gazing down at swaying reeds beneath the tides, momentarily unsure if they are fresh new leaves or restless souls of plants long gone.
A wizened old man wades through water and approaches you. He tilts his head at you, finally speaking after a long moment.
"Friend, spare a few gold coins? As long as I am given passage aboard Thanatos' ferry, I will give you anything in return!" He grabs your arm, and a sharp chill abruptly shoots down your spine.
To be honest, you want nothing more to do with the supernatural for a long time.
"Thank you, young friend." He takes the coin, looks forlornly at the world still untouched by the River of Souls, and disappears into the torrential depths.

The abruptly-stopped dinghy splashes waves upon the sea's surface. Under starlight, you catch a glimpse of jagged rocks ahead. Phagousa's kin lie scattered among them, a haunting dirge clouding your mind.
Sea monsters charmed by the song surround the rocks, while your dinghy is trapped by a school of fish, caught between misfortunes.
Before the fragile boat is crushed under the pressure, you have to do something and escape a watery grave.
You pour the precious honey brew into the sea, its drifting nectar intoxicating the sea monsters. Even the singing Titankin are momentarily distracted as they lick their lips.
The tactic seems to be successful, but the greedy sea is far from sated.

The Titankins, unable to resist, leap into the sea and scramble for the honey brew, while the fish drawn by song return whence they come. You carefully steer past the rocks — amidst the drunken throng of Titankins, the treasures of the sea sparkle with radiance.

You sing of Phagousa's legend, from the moment of birth to the revelry of the present. Amid the melody, the intoxicated Titankins open a path for you, presenting treasures sunk to the bottom as your reward.
You attempt to craft a graceful melody, but your clumsy singing drives even the fish away. The enraged Titankins surge towards you, intent on silencing this heart-wrenching tune.
You take a deep breath, mustering all your strength in your rowing, ignoring the fishy stench that has splattered onto the boat, steering it straight for the submerged reef.
As expected, the dinghy splinters into shreds. Phagousa's kins fish you from the water, tossing you onto the shore with disdain.
You take a deep breath, mustering all your strength in your rowing, ignoring the fishy stench that has splattered onto the boat, steering it straight for the submerged reef.
When you awaken, the sun is already pouring its light over the ocean. The shattered boat is inexplicably laden with treasures — a tribute from the sea to braves.

You recall the melodies of wandering bards, slapping the oar against the side of your dinghy to create an accompanying cue as you regale epic tales of heroes from ages past. Drawn by your song, the once-turbulent sea turns tranquil.
The tactic seems to be successful, but the greedy sea is far from sated.

In the depths of Loukas' prison, your cellmate is hatching a "precise" jailbreak plan.
As punishment for assassinating the tyrant, everyone here will be cast into the arena to be fed to the lions the next time Aquila opens their eyes.

"Oronyx above, we offer all we have in exchange for our lives. Before the tyrant pushes us onto the gallows in their wrath, may you grant us a miracle to deliver us, your humbled disciples." You all place your worldly possessions on the tray, even gold teeth.
Nothing happens.
Perhaps Oronyx is still dreaming? Or are there too many people praying to them? How about trying the other two Fate Titans?
Beneath the Veil of Evernight, time shows you the ancient past, an era without prisons or tyrants. The prison's stone walls crumble before your eyes, and you all stride freely into the world beyond.
A faint sliver of light engulfs your offerings, swallowed by the gaping chasm on the prison floor. A raging river surges below, but leaping in seems the much better option than waiting to die here.

Amidst low whispers that bridge the divide, the blessing of the Gate of Infinity reveals itself to you. The once-sealed prison opens itself, and all who were imprisoned here by the tyrant see the mesmerizing night sky.
The Scale of Justice's blessing always comes at a cost. The instant the prison gates swing open, the patrolling guards catch sight of you as well.
Sharp shadows shred the prison's stone walls, piercing winds chill to the bone — the Scale of Justice's blessing ends here.

This is your first time leaving your homeland of Okhema. The light weight of your armor lifts your spirits. You shoulder a shoddily-crafted spear discarded by its smith, and heroic poems hummed by traveling bards play over and over in your mind.
Share a drink with waves that are the manifestation of Phagousa on the sea and venture into the nether realm in search of your dead lover. One day, there will be a spot for you as well.
You hear that Castrum Kremnos is holding a new tournament. Kephale above, it appears you are destined to seize your inaugural glory there.
What a warrior! Even the local spectators at Castrum Kremnos can't help but cheer you on.
A hero who believes in failing isn't a hero? No matter how much one loses, one shouldn't lose money, right?

You advance smoothly through every round of Castrum Kremnos' tournament. Alas, the King's Aegis' intervention stops your progress. But a hero must not give up. Kephale above, you carry the shield given to you by your comrade, pressing forth on your journey across Amphoreus.
In Janusopolis' temple, you seek a prophecy from its priests: Where should one go, if one wanted to be a hero?
Word has it that a perilous expedition with one's life on the line is about to begin. You board a ship, anticipating adventurous stories of the uncharted.
That is a monster that feeds on both humans and livestock. As it slumbers, you lunge forward and pierce it in its eye.
You all lure the howling behemoth into the trap, but it breaks free of its fetters in its dying moments, launching a final, desperate lunge at the group.

As the years pass, you return to your hometown once more, battered and scarred. You look out the window. Kephale's radiance still embraces the holy city, yet poems carried by the wind have already spread your renown far and wide.

You were once a hero, but all heroes eventually face their twilight. Children would always tug at you to mesmerize them with your feats of past, pretending to be heroes on an expedition with you, defeating wooden monsters adorned in painted scribbles.
With a swing of your wooden stick, the children playing monsters would fall dramatically to the ground, followed by gleeful giggles.
A chill rises from your toes. At the end of the tide, Thanatos' longship will ferry you on a journey into the next life.

In the breeding records of the Caprists, you discover a statistical error. Creatures created in an environment with controlled temperatures show a deformity rate lower than its standard rates by 3% when their size expands.
But you are fully aware that this is related to the current foundation of your research. Once this goes public, all existing academic progress will be destroyed.

Not to mention that the one who made the erroneous entry is a prominent scholar of the Grove. You look at the tiny critters multiplying before you, conflicted over whether to correct the error in the breeding scheme.
What's wrong with this data? It's already been in use for dozens of years. You must be the one who's wrong.
Your conclusion garners the support of many esteemed seniors, but your peers in your school grow more estranged from you.
The deformed chimera gnaws off a piece of stone wall, romping about in the room. Because of the erroneous fusion of two chimerae, the inorganic monster sprouts spines, growling menacingly at you all.

Having achieved fame, you suddenly realize that this is the result of a stroke of luck from the erroneous data that you ignored all those years ago. If this matter were to get out, you would surely be unceremoniously cast out of the Grove.
Looking at the monster before you, you decide to...

You raise an iron rod and fight the crazed chimera for three bouts, finally ending up with a pile of scrap metal. You now understand what the scrap metal pieces your mentor had you deal with really are...
Grappling with every ounce of your strength, you manage to lock up the crazed chimera. It will be shown as the results of animal reintroduction into the wild at the Caprism school's exhibition.
Your scandal has become a hot topic within the Grove, but at least future scholars won't be obstructed by such blunders again.

You find yourself on a strange chessboard. Two hazy figures sway above, throwing out wooden sticks from their hands in order, and moving your position. Your body is round and smooth, just like... a Cyclicality chesspiece.
The Fate Titans' disciples model their actions after yours, emulating the change between life and reincarnation.

You leap quickly across the chessboard, from the snow-laden northern domain to the center of the Chrysos War. You begin to question the role you are playing. Meanwhile, another chesspiece stands at the other end of the battlefield. Oh, you're both now generals of two opposing city-states, about to engage in an intense battle!
Talanton above, what is the price you're willing to pay for victory?
You know this bet to be somewhat dangerous — even your hand holding the chesspiece is trembling. But your courage will earn a Titan's response.
On the field, wealth is most insignificant. You are raring for action, ready to knock the enemy off the chessboard.
You offer the treasure in your hands, akin to a priest of the Temple of the Three Fates beseeching the Titans for protection.
The two chess players toss out their wooden sticks at the same time. The fate of the battle will hinge on only these two pieces.

"Step right up! Feast your eyes on the finest relics, all excavated straight from the ruins of the Era Chrysea! If it's fake, I'll pay you back tenfold!" A masked merchant calls out, their voice cutting through the marketplace bustle.

You sift through the shelves and, sure enough, spot some real treasures. But after sneaking a glance at the prices, you instinctively tighten your grip on your wallet — looks like it's time for some haggling.
"By Zagreus above! I risked life and limb to recover... Oh, I mean, acquire these relics! You can't expect me to leave out the danger fee!"
You hesitate, unsure of what to do.
"And just like that, it's yours! A pleasure doing business with you!"
"Ah, too bad! Another prized treasure just left the shelves. If you've got your eyes on something, don't wait too long!" The merchant prods.
"Lucky you! We're running a very special promotion right now — hesitate, and you might never see a deal like this again!" The merchant prods.
"Ah, too bad! Another prized treasure just left the shelves. If you've got your eyes on something, don't wait too long!" The merchant prods.

"Lucky you! We're running a very special promotion right now — hesitate, and you might never see a deal like this again!" The merchant prods.

Your hood is yanked off, and in an instant, your senses are assaulted — a grand circular arena, a frenzied crowd, and corpses strewn across the bloodstained sand. Your instincts scream danger, but at least there's one silver lining — you're still breathing.

This is the arena of Castrum Kremnos, where the citizens of Castrum Kremnos exalt in slaughter, celebrating yet another triumph for their bloodthirsty king. And you? You are nothing more than the loot, a doomed offering in this twisted carnival of death.

The bronze gate rumbles open, revealing the beast, a towering lion with ten burning eyes. It catches the bloody scent of your wounds. Its enormous fangs, thick as a human forearm, grinding together with an ominous metallic screech.

"Listen up, kitty — keep acting up, and I'll knock your front teeth out!" The giant lion freezes, its ten eyes blinking in sheer disbelief. Then, its shock twists into unrelenting fury. With a deafening roar, it lunges straight for you, jaws unhinging.

"A little kitty like this? Ha! I could take on ten more!" You have no idea what possessed you to blurt that out, but the giant lion seems to have understood the taunt — its ten eyes blaze with bloodshot fury.

You unleash a barrage of insults, each one sharper than the last, your body moving instinctively into taunting stances you don't even remember learning. Whatever possessed you, it's working — the beast has snapped.
The talkative ones die first. You drop the theatrics, shift into a battle stance, and steel yourself for the bloodbath ahead.
The last fight had already drained you. You just want this over with.

The police aircar weaves through the tangled lanes of drone traffic, touching down smoothly atop a three-thousand-story skyscraper. Seven minutes have passed since the emergency call, and as a High-Risk Biohazard Disposal Specialist, you've finally made it to the crime scene.

"It's a shapeshifter. It's already tricked a few of our officers — stay alert." The on-site officer sends a data packet straight to your neural link. The next thing you know, a stabbing pain rips through your skull.
"Ahahaha! Got another one!" The officer's body liquefies into a writhing mass of slime — then reshapes itself into a giant, mocking middle finger.
You flash a knowing smirk — what your slimy opponent doesn't realize is that, just moments ago, you hijacked the neural link and slipped a virus into its system. Outwitted and outclassed.
Not the best start to this mission... but a tactical retreat is better than a reckless demise. You can deal with it another day.
A robed friar stops you. She carries a weighty brass scale — likely a follower of Talanton.
You're in no mood for justice or balance, ready to wave her off, but she raises the scale toward you before you can speak.

"I walk in the world, spreading the word of Talanton's equilibrium. You may entrust a wish to this scale — place it upon one side, and if your wish is fulfilled, then the other side will bear a matching reward. Both shall be yours."
If even Talanton's followers are resorting to mystical sales pitches, times must be rough. Then again... no harm in trying, right?
"I can already sense wealth gathering at one end of the scale. When the balance is restored, I will return to you." With a faint smile, the friar turns and walks away.
"I can already sense power gathering at one end of the scale. When the balance is restored, I will return to you." With a faint smile, the friar turns and walks away.
"I can already sense wisdom gathering at one end of the scale. When the balance is restored, I will return to you." With a faint smile, the friar turns and walks away.
"You've passed up a golden opportunity, but perhaps your scale was already in perfect balance." The friar gives you a knowing nod of approval.

A burst of heat from the stove pipe inflates the sheepskin airbag in an instant. The sugar-glazed propellers creak and groan in delight. After one last check of the cotton candy-wrapped aircraft, you lift off, wobbling into the sky.

The tragedy of the skyship is no secret, but you're convinced its downfall came from being too conspicuous. With that in mind, you took the smarter route — miniaturization. And for an extra touch of brilliance, you used cotton candy to disguise yourself as a drifting puff of clouds.

From up here, valleys and rivers unfold beneath you, a breathtaking panorama. You feel the refreshing chill of a breeze unique to high altitudes. But with every inch you climb, so does the risk of catching Aquila's attention. A choice must be made.
You're already standing above <unbreak>99.99%</unbreak> of Amphoreus. Perhaps it's time to descend. The ground is far more dependable.
You've witnessed sights that few ever will. As for the even grander views beyond? Those are for the reckless to pursue.
Your mind is set. Once your feet touch solid ground again, you're reopening a cotton candy shop. And you're swearing off flying for good.
You sold off your family-run cotton candy shop at Bulsa and drowned yourself in debt to build the ultimate flying machine — not to hover at this pathetic altitude listening to sparrows chirp.
The winds grow more erratic, tossing your machine like a drifting leaf. Strips of cotton candy are ripped away by the turbulence. You know what this means — Aquila is searching for you.

But Aquila has underestimated your ingenuity. The machine's engine is also a cotton candy machine. You immediately crank out many fresh layers of cotton candy, reinforcing your disguise. You even make enough to sneak a snack.
Do you ascend further?
What kind of adventurer backs down when faced with danger? If you were the type to play it safe, you'd still be on the ground, spinning cotton candy for children.

A bolt of lightning splits the heavens, the air thick with the sharp tang of scorch — Aquila is furious. Their hundred eyes have failed them, and in a fit of rage, they unleash a relentless storm of divine thunder, determined to obliterate you.
Your machine is a flying tinderbox. One stray spark, and your cloud-like disguise will ignite into a fiery inferno.
Do you ascend further?

Maybe it was the relentless drive of an adventurer pushing you forward — or maybe you just couldn't stomach the idea of returning to the ground to spin cotton candy. Either way, you throw caution to the wind and surge straight into the heart of the thunderstorm above you.
When the storm finally subsides, the air carries a lingering sweetness. Down below, children stare in wide-eyed wonder as soft tufts of cotton candy drift from the sky like rain...
The Grove of Epiphany has issued its Intern Scholar Examination — an open call across all of Amphoreus. After twenty long years of academic toil, you know this is a chance you cannot let slip away.

The competition is staggering, with countless hopefuls vying for just three precious spots. You force yourself to calm the excitement buzzing in your veins — focus. The real question is: which of your research projects should you submit?
Your scholarly pursuits span a dizzying array of fields, but in academia, raw merit isn't everything — Submitting something the panel likes is just as crucial.
The Caprism reviewer might find this particular outcome intriguing... but the title? A bit questionable. Do chimeras even have postnatal physiology?

A week later, the Grove of Epiphany delivers its verdict — a polite rejection. "Your research holds immense academic significance! However, it does not align with our current primary research direction. Your credentials have been added to our talent database, and we look forward to potential collaboration in the future."
"So be it. If the Grove of Epiphany can't recognize true genius, then I want no part of them." You say the words with defiance... but as you do, a lone tear betrays you, sliding down your cheek.
Bathing is undoubtedly important, but presenting it as a groundbreaking scientific discovery? That might be a stretch. Then again, maybe there's a bath-loving reviewer on the panel?

A week later, the Grove of Epiphany delivers its verdict — a polite rejection. "Your research holds immense academic significance! However, it does not align with our current primary research direction. Your credentials have been added to our talent database, and we look forward to potential collaboration in the future."
"So be it. If the Grove of Epiphany can't recognize true genius, then I want no part of them." You say the words with defiance... but as you do, a lone tear betrays you, sliding down your cheek.
The Caprism reviewer might find this particular outcome intriguing... but the title? A bit questionable. Do chimeras even have postnatal physiology?

A week later, the unthinkable happens — an acceptance letter from the Grove of Epiphany. "Congratulations! Your research has successfully passed the selection process. We are pleased to invite you for an interview at the Grove of Epiphany."
Bathing is undoubtedly important, but presenting it as a groundbreaking scientific discovery? That might be a stretch. Then again, maybe there's a bath-loving reviewer on the panel?

A week later, the unthinkable happens — an acceptance letter from the Grove of Epiphany. "Congratulations! Your research has successfully passed the selection process. We are pleased to invite you for an interview at the Grove of Epiphany."
Outrageous! Researching golden blood — is that even ethical? But... you have to admit, the subject is rather fascinating.

A week later, the unthinkable happens — an acceptance letter from the Grove of Epiphany. "Congratulations! Your research has successfully passed the selection process. We are pleased to invite you for an interview at the Grove of Epiphany."

They say only the rarest of scholars reach the interview stage, yet as you step into the waiting hall — crammed tighter than Marmoreal Market during a festival sale, you can't help but marvel at the sheer number of bright minds in Amphoreus.

So far, not a single person has passed. Those emerging from the soundproofed interview rooms are either weeping uncontrollably like lost children or ripping their papers to shreds in pure rage. No doubt about it — the judges are experts in breaking wills.

"Applicant <unbreak>108</unbreak>, please enter." The voice shatters your train of thought. You wipe the sweat from your brow, steady your breath, and carefully push open the heavy wooden door to the interview room.
Determined to leave a lasting first impression, you toss your demonstration model straight at the interviewer's shiny bald head.

The interviewer fires a relentless barrage of questions, each one hitting like a precision strike. You barely manage to utter the first syllable of your answer before his brow furrows so deeply it could crush a fly.
Your confidence crumbles with each passing second. Under the interviewer's withering sarcasm and razor-sharp critiques, you can feel yourself shrinking, desperately wishing for an escape.
As expected, you don't even receive a rejection letter. It's as if the reviewer even forgot that you never existed.

Every question lands squarely in your wheelhouse. With unshakable confidence, you answer fluently, words flowing like a torrential river. At the height of your enthusiasm, you even leap to your feet, passionately scrawling equations across the blackboard.
Your sheer intellect and mastery leave the interviewer speechless. With rare, unfiltered admiration, he declares you the most outstanding candidate he's seen in years.
Right there on the spot, you're granted the title of Intern Scholar. And beyond that, he assures you that your rise to full scholar status is only a matter of time in the Grove.

"This is what you call a challenge for the Grove's reviewers? Ha! Any half-decent reviewer could handle this!" With a dismissive scoff, the reviewer throws you out the door, but keeps the gift you brought.

Three days later, a letter arrives from the Grove of Epiphany: "Congratulations! You have successfully passed the interview. You are now an Intern Scholar of the Grove of Epiphany. Please bring your invitation and report to the Grove."
It seems that, no matter the world, understanding the art of human interaction is crucial.

You follow the Woven Trail, its winding paths twisting in intricate, almost deliberate patterns. Passing through the White Dryad Woods, where philosophical debates took place, you finally arrive at the most sacred place in all of Amphorean academia — the Grove of Epiphany's Library of Philia.

Here lies the vast majority of Amphoreus's books. To you, it's as if a hopeless drinker has stumbled upon Phagousa's legendary wine cellar — the sheer temptation to lose yourself in this sea of wisdom is overwhelming.
As a scholar of the Grove, even if the title still bears the "intern" prefix, you have the privilege to read any book in this library. So, where do you start?

You consume the text with a hunger so ravenous, it's as if your mind itself has been starved. Each word, is like rainfall upon a drought-stricken field, quenching your insatiable thirst for knowledge.
With this formidable library at your disposal, and your own brilliant intellect to guide you, who's to say that one day you won't rise to the ranks of the Seven Sages?

The dromas lets out a deep, contented burp after swallowing the last chunk of redsoil — a clear signal that the day's work is about to begin. As the most renowned dromas handler in Hattusili, it falls upon you to assign tasks to these towering beasts.

This year has been a season of abundance. The fields overflow with freshly harvested crops, stacked high and ready for transport. But just as the last sheaf is gathered, the distant call of the harbor reaches your ears — the overseas trade fleet has arrived, bringing timber and stone in need of urgent delivery.
To transport crops from the farmland or to transport materials from the port? You find yourself lost in thought.
Crops spoil quickly. It makes sense to head for the farmland first.
With a low rumble, the dromas sways as it carries you off.
Storage fees at the port can be costly. Perhaps the materials should come first.
With a low rumble, the dromas sways as it carries you off.
Decisions, decisions... In the end, you settle on the hardest path of all — both. The dromas will haul crops during the day and transport materials at night.
Your heart is harder than stone. Then don't be surprised when Georios delivers your punishment.

Before you stand two doors — one ancient and solemn, cast in bronze. The other radiant and opulent, sculpted from gold. You've been staring at them, unmoving, for an entire day — ever since you wandered too deep into this twisting labyrinth.

As an adventurer who has roamed the farthest reaches of the world, you've seen the Janus priests use their mystical "passages" to bypass insurmountable barriers. But once a gate is opened, there's no going back.
Luckily, you aren't limited to a simple A or B choice. There's always a third option — walking out on your own.
"This has to be one of Janus' tricks!" you mutter before disappearing into the labyrinth's shadows.
You grip the handle tightly, plant your feet, and shove with all your strength. But the moment the door moves, it swings open effortlessly, sending you tumbling inside.

Before your eyes, the two doors liquefy, and the bronze and gold engulfs you like molten lava. You fight to escape, but by the time you claw your way free, your backpack is completely deflated — all your treasures, gone, swallowed by the tide.
You grip the handle tightly, plant your feet, and shove with all your strength. But the moment the door moves, it swings open effortlessly, sending you tumbling inside.

After a brief moment of blindness, your vision clears, and before you stand the same two doors as before. Only this time, your backpack feels heavier. A few new treasures rest inside. It seems you were on the right track, just not quite right enough.

You open your eyes to find yourself amidst waves of golden wheat. A gentle breeze caresses your face as wisps of smoke rise from the chimneys of a distant village. Though the sun is nowhere to be seen in the sky, it radiates a soft, bright glow.
"Hey, fancy seeing you here." A familiar voice comes from behind. You turn around to find that girl, wheat grains stuck to the hem and cuffs of her clothes, as if she's been napping in the fields.
"Ah, just to be clear, I wasn't slacking off. I was just getting some creative inspiration here. Look, I made you this wreath from wheat stalks. It's yours!"

options.text: Thank you, I'll take good care of it.

lines: "Don't you remember?" she laughed, "That's okay, I'll tell you everything, every last detail of the story we wrote together."
"Hehe, no need to thank me! I'm just glad you like it. After all the adventures we've been through together, consider it a little memento."
"Is it a dream, or a memory?" she laughed, "Maybe they're one and the same? Either way, just sit back and enjoy the story."
"How about that? Isn't it wonderful? I love the ending most. It comes with a little touch of fantasy." The girl closes the book, and the heroes and epics all become a page of eternity.
"Well then, I look forward to seeing you again. I'm sure our story will have a romantic ending too ♪"
"Speaking of stories..." The girl conjures up a seemingly familiar, thick book, and its pages rustle in the wind.
"What kind of story would you like to hear today?"

"...And so the story ends. The threat at the kingdom's borders was quelled, and the hero's deeds would be sung for ages to come. Yet none would know that the legendary 'evil dragon' had quietly become the maiden who stood by the hero's side..."
"...And so the story ends. The king who sought immortality would never die, but his youth slowly withered away with time... The moral of the story is: Be very, very careful what you wish for."

"...And so the story ends. The fallen heroes returned from the nether realm, and the ravaged villages were restored. Everyone joined hands, singing and dancing around the bonfire until twilight's end..."
As you approach the ruins of a city-state, Aquila brings down heavy rain. You wander around in the downpour until finally finding shelter in a nearby cave.
As you watch droplets trickle down the protruding stone spikes, a wave of melancholy washes over you, until footsteps echo from deep within the cave. You're not alone.
"Do you want to ask me about the Sealing Wax?" The old man reveals himself, his eyes burning like torches.

"If you want, you can come back to find me in these caves anytime. This is where I live." The old man tightens the cloth bag on his shoulder. "Perhaps soon, you'll understand the benefits of living in solitude."

Once again, you arrive at the ruins of the city-state. Following the familiar path, you return to the cave where you once took shelter from the rain. The old man stands at the entrance to welcome you. He still looks spirited, while your face bears the marks of wind and frost.

"Looks like you've been through a lot." He smiles, his wrinkles like the weathered bark of an old tree. "Now you must understand that there's no place for stateless folks like us out there. And I want nothing to do with either the black tide or the privileged elite."
"Here, take this Sealing Wax and come live with me in the cave forever. There are many others here..." The old man unties the sack from his back.

Hardship and failure have worn down your edges, while calamity and strife have crushed your spirit. As you take the Sealing Wax from the elder's hand, a faint glow emerges from deep within the cave, like a burning flame.
Since then, you've never seen the blue sky outside the cave again.

Though you faced failure before, you haven't lost your courage and hope. The old man flashes a gap-toothed smile as you shoulder your well-packed bag, ready to challenge the land where black tides surge once more.
Since then, you've never returned to those caves.
You're walking down a deserted country road with a bag full of Sealing Wax. Suddenly, a huge purple spherical object, which looks just like a grape, jumps out...
"This mountain's mine to claim, and this path's mine to... wait, that's not right..." says the purple grape. Apparently it is a living thing.
"I am the Amphorean God of Sealing Wax." It puts its hands on its hips and puffs out its chest. "Give me your Sealing Wax, and I'll synthesize a super powerful one for you!"
"What a fine treasure! It's yours now." The purple grape spits out a unique Sealing Wax, then vanishes like the wind.
"What fine treasures! They're yours now." The purple grape spits out tons of Curios, then vanishes like the wind.
"Ouch, old Bartholos' back can't take this anymore!" The purple grape spits out tons of Balance Coins, then vanishes like the wind.
In the Garden of Life, as a trainer, you are checking on the little chimera's work.
"Your performance is below standard again today. Can't you learn from your coworkers and try to keep up with their task progress?" You interrogate the little chimera.

"But... boss, keeping up with the schedule is impossible!" The little chimera begins to argue for itself, "Because to catch up with other coworkers' progress, I first need to catch up with the current progress. But once I catch up with the current progress, the others will have moved even further ahead!"
"At this rate, I'll never catch up with my coworkers!" The little chimera declared blatantly.
Moved by this well-reasoned argument, you decide to ease up on employee performance metrics. The little chimera beams gleefully.
The little chimera has a point, and you quickly find a way to solve the problem:

Why not just give other chimeras time off and let the little chimera who's behind schedule continue working? Working while others are on holiday is also a form of overtime. You've dubbed this method the "Theory of Relative Overtime."
"What's all this mumbo-jumbo?" You couldn't understand the little chimera's reasoning at all, but you know one thing for sure: No food to eat if today's work isn't finished!
"Awoo~" The little chimera trudges back to its workstation, ready for another round of overtime.
As a skilled debater from the Grove of Epiphany, you quickly point out the issue with the little chimera:
While work progress can indeed be infinitely divided, it doesn't mean it requires infinite time. As the progress gaps become shorter and shorter, the time needed converges into a finite level.
"Awoo~" The little chimera trudges back to its workstation, ready for another round of overtime.

After hearing the little chimera's words, you sink into deep contemplation. Yeah, what's the meaning of work, anyway? Life is finite, but work is endless. What the chimera does is nothing more than repeatedly pushing a boulder up the mountain...
While you seem to have grasped some profound truth, the little chimera has long since slacked off during your philosophical moment.

As a Ruin Strider, you roam among crumbling walls far from civilization, with a particular fondness for ancient tombs buried deep underground. Some say you're just after the dead's treasures, but you couldn't care less.
"Click... THUD!" A mechanism triggers, and the tomb's stone door comes crashing down. You raise your torch, illuminating the dark room ahead, where an inscription on the wall catches your eye:
"Those who have reached this place possess extraordinary courage. The Gods of Three Fates who govern destiny shall bestow upon you a reward, which marks the beginning of your legend."
At the far end of the room, a chest silently awaits. Inside lies what you desire most...
You lift the lid of the chest and take out the divine treasure that belongs to you. A gaze seems to linger from behind, or perhaps it's just a warm breeze.

After obtaining the divine treasure from the ancient tomb, you've been through countless adventures: Rescuing a refugee mother and child from Black Tide Creatures, helping the Grove transport endangered plant seeds, and even briefly getting involved in the strife between Castrum Kremnos and Okhema. The treasure always proves useful.
One night, you sit by the lake at the foot of the snowy mountain, toying with the divine treasure. The moon is hidden behind thick clouds, with only a few dim rays of light seeping through.
"Thou hast proven thyself worthy." A gentle whisper drifts by your ear, from one of the Gods of Three Fates, unknown which. "Thy virtue shall add strength to the treasure."
You nod in agreement to the voice. As the thick clouds disperse, soft moonlight pours down, and your treasure seems to have undergone a change...
You make a request to the voice. The thick clouds part, and gentle moonlight pours down, revealing something at your feet...
You humbly decline this power. The thick clouds disperse as gentle moonlight pours down. When you open your eyes, the divine treasure has vanished, but something is left at your feet.

After obtaining a more powerful divine treasure, you achieve many great deeds, and your bond with it grows even stronger. Poets compose ballads, spreading tales of your feats. A sacred sense of purpose rises from deep within: You are destined to forge true legends with it.
Myths and legends weave a web, guiding you to your fated destination. You climb to the mountain's peak at night, to the place closest to the stars and gods, and kneel in prayer.
"Few have made it this far." The voice echoes from the stars, "You can still rise higher, but it will come at a certain cost..."

You cut your palm with the ritual blade, and golden blood drips from your fingertips into the lake. Legend has it that an ancient sage once traded their own eye to Oronyx in exchange for the power to foresee the future. A hero themselves is the greatest sacrifice.

Your wounds heal in an instant. The pantheon has accepted this offering. The thick clouds part, letting gentle moonlight pour down as warmth and power surge through your body. You feel more invigorated than ever before, like a vessel filled to the brim.

There was a tale told in the city of Icatus: A carpenter crafted a sculpture so masterful it seemed divine, yet he lived forever in its shadow, never able to create anything better. On his deathbed, he destroyed his masterpiece with his own hands and died with a smile on his face.

The divine treasure is a rare and powerful tool, but it can also become a shackle, an obsession. You beg the gods to take back their blessing. The thick clouds disperse as gentle moonlight pours down. When you open your eyes, the divine treasure has vanished, but something is left at your feet.
Moonlight shines upon your path of departure. When the time is right, you can still rise higher.
Your voice grows increasingly hoarse. It's the gods' subtle refusal. You smile wryly and take the hint, getting up to leave. Your time hasn't come yet.

Your voice grows ever more resonant. The divine has accepted this offering. The thick clouds part, letting gentle moonlight pour down as warmth and power surge through your body. You feel more invigorated than ever before, like a vessel filled to the brim.

The Month of Gate marks the beginning of a year. During this month, people discard possessions they no longer need, burn items connected to those they were bonded with, declaring a break from the past and facing the future head-on.

In the previous Month of Mourning, war devoured your dearest friend. The soldiers brought back his body atop their shields, and Thanatos has taken him into their palm. People recommend you attend this year's Enkindle Ceremony. It's time for you to begin a new life.
"May Thanatos be kind to my mother." The stern-faced man tosses a clay bowl into the fire pit, then walks over and pats your shoulder. It's your turn.

You take out the amulet given to you by your dear friend and cast it into the fire pit. It was the memento of how your friendship began. Your longing rises slowly with the flames and smoke until it disappears into thin air.
You pick up the painted clay tablet and cast it into the fire pit. That was countless days and nights of hard work. Your longing rises with the flames and smoke, until it all vanishes into thin air.

With a wave of your hand, the workers bring over wardrobes, wooden crates, and other belongings, dumping them all into the fire pit with heavy thuds. Memories rise with the flames and smoke, slowly dissipating into the air until they vanish.
Move on from the past? Never! You dig your nails into your arm, drawing blood, and swear to everyone present: you'll turn this pain into burning rage and incinerate everything that has ever hurt you.
You pick up your spear and shield. In this Month of Strife, you will march with the army to slay the enemy's dearest friends and burn their homeland. Destruction can only be repaid by destruction.
"Clang! Bang!" The sounds of clashing weapons echo across the training grounds as the Holy City Guards carry out their routine drills.

Thrust, upward slash, change of guard, disarm... You execute a flawless sequence of attacks, and your opponent's iron sword clatters to the ground. As you shake your arm, sore from gripping the wooden sword for far too long, your observing colleagues burst into applause and admiration.

"Your swordplay has improved tremendously. Once you complete the Final Trial, you'll be the undisputed choice for Captain of the Holy City Guards." The sword instructor's eyes gleamed with approval, "Your opponent will be a Kin of Strife. Think you can win?"

You shake your head, knowing there are very few who can match your skill level. Self-study is the only true path forward. Using wooden dummies as imaginary opponents, you practice your swordplay. By the end of the day, the broken dummies have piled up like a mountain.

With a rallying cry, skilled warriors from the army gathered to volunteer as your sparring partners. By the end of the day, your defeated opponents formed a long line, and your face was covered in sweat and smiles.

Comfortable training is still just training. Only real combat can drive one forward. You venture out of the city alone with your sword, diving into ruins occupied by Black Tide Creatures. As the day ends, you stagger back to the city gates, your wildly beating heart now stronger and more tenacious.

The principles of swordsmanship are no different from mathematics. Even the strongest body needs a mind to guide it. You visited a Helkolithist Sage to exchange insights and hone your skills. As the day ends, you're drenched in sweat. Training the mind proves no easier than training the body.

An epiphany dawns in your mind, like sunlight streaming through a window.

The promised day has arrived. With your sword in hand, you approach your formidable foe, towering like a mountain, its bronze mask gleaming in the sunlight. Citizens gather around, bearing witness to this epic confrontation...

Poets and those facing death often speak of the River of Souls. Its waters were both serene and turbulent. On this shore lie scattered souls of the dead who haven't crossed, while the opposite bank leads to flower fields, symbolizing rebirth. When the ferryman carries the dead toward the other shore, the waters are as calm as a mirror. But should a soul attempt to cross alone, they'd be swallowed by the raging currents.

The balance of death has been broken. At some point, Thanatos ceased to ferry souls. On the <unbreak>2,778</unbreak>th day of being trapped on the Nethershore, you decide to take matters into your own hands.

As a captain, you've witnessed thousand-meters-high rogue waves in the Eastern Seas. Compared to those, the River of Souls is just an oversized bathtub. The not-entirely-dead crew gather around you, awaiting orders. Once you sail to the other shore and fall into Thanatos's hands, you'll all find your true death.
The will of the gods often manifests in ways that need interpretation. You might see the current situation as a subtle rejection. Perhaps you still need to wait until the day you're truly prepared...

As a sailor, you know all too well the dangers of water, but thankfully your ship "died" along with you in that shipwreck. You call out to your fellow sailors to gather the scattered deck pieces, piecing the ship back in shape together.

As you stand at the bow, the folded sails automatically fill with wind. This is the legendary ghost ship. The calm waters suddenly erupt into massive waves, and you sail head-on into them, like a warrior charging towards a giant dragon.

"Take us with you! Why should you alone savor the sweet embrace of death?" The fallen souls in the River of Souls reach out their hands, trying to puncture holes in your ship's hull, and among them are even Phagousa's creations. You and your crew frantically strike with wooden oars, but struggle to fend off the siege...

A gentle breeze calmed the towering waves, carrying the scent of Antila flowers. A young girl wielding a giant scythe approached slowly from downstream of the River of Souls, her boots creating ripples on the water's surface. Her color resembles that of lavender.
"Sorry I'm late. From now on, life and death shall never part." She raises her hand, and that ethereal fragrance guides you forward. At last, you fall into sweet death.

Objects used by Titans often inherit a portion of their divine power. You firmly believe that those who failed met with giant waves because they hadn't found the right vessel. With this conviction, you led the sailors to search along the coast until finally discovering that ownerless ferry.

The sailing procedure was pretty much the same. You left the shore and quickly approached the middle of the river. The calm water suddenly erupted into massive waves, throwing you all overboard. Seems like divine authority isn't something mortals can imitate.

"Come, come, sink with us into the depths!" The fallen souls in the River of Souls reach out their hands, trying to drag you under the water, and among them are even Phagousa's creations. One by one, crew members vanish beneath the surface as you swim forward desperately, not daring to look back...

A gentle breeze calmed the towering waves, carrying the scent of Antila flowers. A young girl wielding a giant scythe approached slowly from downstream of the River of Souls, her boots creating ripples on the water's surface. Her color resembles that of lavender.
"Sorry I'm late. From now on, life and death shall never part." She raises her hand, and that ethereal fragrance guides you forward. At last, you fall into sweet death.
Given enough time, you might be able to piece together a bigger ship with it.

You are a Hinge Hunter, a Galaxy Ranger who views Intellitrons as mortal enemies. You have sworn an oath to make the remnants of the Emperor pay for their crimes. That was your mission then, and it remains your mission now.

You pilot your arrow-shaped ship through the stars. On a graveyard planet, you find a mountain made of Intellitron parts. The Emperor's War left behind thousands of graves, claiming both organic and inorganic lives alike.

A mangled domestic robot crawls out from the wreckage. It drags itself along with its only two remaining limbs, display screen blinking red. The apron around its waist is a sign that it once served a human family.
You reach for the giant hammer on your back. Is this Intellitron still the target of your mission?
As the battle ends, the domestic robot flips open a cover and splashes coolant right in your face. Judging by its expression, this was probably its final, desperate strike.
"Darn it, are you actually not afraid of water?" Those are the Intellitron's final words before it shuts down for good.
You snap your weapon case shut and walk away. A Galaxy Ranger never swings their blade at an opponent who can no longer fight back. The same goes for hammers and guns.

You are a Hinge Hunter, a Galaxy Ranger who views Intellitrons as mortal enemies. You have sworn an oath to make the remnants of the Emperor pay for their crimes. That was your mission then, and it remains your mission now.
You pilot your arrow-shaped ship through the stars. In an abandoned space station, you find a mechanical soldier occupying the main lobby.

It has six legs, each equipped with an open flamethrower. Its left arm crackles with electricity, while its right has been replaced with a Matter Annihilation Cannon. No doubt about it: this is a classic "Human Hunter."
You reach for the giant hammer on your back. Is this Intellitron still the target of your mission?
You crush that mechanical soldier to pieces with your giant hammer. Survivors burst out of the safe room, cheering and dancing. Maybe this space station won't be "abandoned" for much longer.
You've hunted enough of these small-fry. You decide to save your strength for the fights that actually matter.
