You pilot your arrow-shaped ship through the stars. On the edge of a star system, you discover a factory planet that's still in operation. Black oil flows through its rivers, and massive chimneys tower like mountain ranges.

Standard combat robots roll off the assembly line like cans of soup. You scale a massive tower made of gears. At its peak, an energy core glows as bright as the sun. If you take it out, you shut down the whole line.
"Organic contamination detected..." A section of the tower suddenly straightens up, revealing itself to be a combat colossus the size of a mountain...
You holster your giant hammer as the gear tower comes crashing down. For at least a few Amber Eras, the organic life nearby can finally get a good night's sleep.
Taking out this whole planet by yourself is a bit too risky. You gather some scattered parts for evidence and set a course for the Skybow Arsenal to call for backup.

You're a Masked Fool. You might not have the sharpest punchlines among the tavern regulars, but you live for the drinksmith's custom-mixed jokes. They're as satisfying as that first big stretch in the morning.

You push open the tavern doors. The drinksmith is gone, leaving only a bunch of wispae and a few odd-looking mixed jokes on the counter. One is a blue-flamed plasma, another is crystal clear and shimmers with metaphorical light, and the last is a cup of bubbling, scalding black mud.
Looks like you'll have to help yourself today.

At first, you don't react, just tasting a bit of sweetness. But then, an incredible power surges through you. You feel like you could fly into the sky and punch the moon until it explodes. You're absolutely fired up.

You down the metaphorical light, and your body starts shifting within the symbolic realm. You're no longer human. You're a reed, then iron, then the sum of all social relations. You keep changing forms right in front of everyone, only returning to your original self when the bar closes.
You drink the cup of black mud... honestly, this thing needs a warning label. Before long, your stomach starts staging a protest, and your face twists into a grimace that's definitely not a smile.
Oh boy, looks like you've had a bit too much bad humor, or what we call "cringe jokes." You've got a massive headache from all the joking, and you won't be laughing again for a long, long time.
You're a desk jockey in Duomension City, trading your finite life for a finite paycheck. After surviving the fourth "crunch week" of the month, you finally get a half-day off.
You're wandering the streets of Planarcadia when an ice cream truck appears. Standing behind it is a strange guy in a top hat, looking like he just stepped out of a circus.

"Vacations are what segment our lives," the strange vendor says. "When you're a student, one segment is four months. When you work, one segment is seven days. And if you're a real unlucky soul, who knows how long a segment lasts!"

"But I can sell you these instead." He flips open a storage chest to reveal a collection of colorful vacations. They're plump and shimmering, looking like they'd burst with sweet nectar if you took a bite.
You shake your head and walk away, never to see that vendor again. At the end of the month, you notice a nice little bonus in your paycheck for all that overtime.
You get into a brawl with the vendor. But just as your ultimate is about to clock him right in the nose, he and his ice cream truck vanish into thin air.
The crowd bursts into applause, and the Wishpower that was meant for him ends up going to you instead.
"Thanks for your business," says the man in the top hat. He hands you an orange-yellow chunk, grinning with teeth of the exact same color.
You're just another netizen in Duomension City. The web is your second home, and your account is your second body. Today, you're out surfing the cyberworld.

"Want to know what it's like to truly live?" an anonymous account asks. "We're all trapped in a massive conspiracy. The CEO is a cyborg in disguise, the Phantasmoon is a lie, and Aha is actually walking among us..."
"I've put the whole truth on this website. Good luck." With that, a glowing link pops up in front of you.
You click the link, only to find it's not some grand conspiracy reveal. It's just a video of ploos dancing. Tons of trashy memetic content floods your brain... Congratulations, you just got "memed."

Nice try being cautious, but it didn't help. You try to close the window, but your system's been hijacked. Your terminal starts blasting ploo dance videos, and your mind is flooded with trashy memetic content... Congratulations, you just got "memed."

Yeah, you didn't click, but cyber-kidnappers don't play by the rules. After a moment, your terminal starts auto-playing ploo dance videos anyway. Trashy memetic content floods your mind... Congratulations, you just got "memed."
You open your eyes, and a wave of heat stings your skin. You drag yourself out from the ruins of a house, surrounded by smoke, dust, and cinders. And fire... purple fire...

Not long ago, monsters known as "Demons From Beyond" descended from the sky. Mothers clutching their children fled screaming, while fathers wielding spears were severed at the waist. Ahatopia, your home, was invaded. And yet, the Phantasmoon merely watched from high above in silence, unmoved.
Suddenly, your fingertips brush against something. It is a blank mask, wearing a smile that isn't quite a smile. It is your ticket to the Phantasmoon Games.

They say that masks choose their own masters. You don't know why its gaze fell upon you, but this mask has undeniably revealed your future, in which you will become a Supplicant, and perhaps even an Aeon. You will possess might, and with it, the authority to rewrite reality.
"Begin the roll-call. Become a Supplicant. Then, change everything." A voice echoes from the depths of your heart. So, how will you use this power?
You quietly take an oath beneath the Phantasmoon, voicing your desires. And so, the final Phantasmoon Games of the Cindearth Age begins...

You open your eyes. Carp riding auspicious clouds fly past the window, followed by the children with kite strings made of dragon tails in their hands. A lightpaw riding a rocket tosses the morning paper and a wispae right through your window.

Who knows how many years have passed since Ahatopia entered the World in Canvas? People chased one another and frolicked within the eternal scroll, never tiring of the fun. The fire that seemed capable of burning up the sky had long since been cast to the back of their minds.

But the jokes eventually ran dry. To add a ripple to a stagnant world, people projected their exaggerated and distorted wishes onto the Phantasmoon Games. Supplicants arbitrarily created new races, locations, and news, only to wipe them away like oil paint. All of these can be summed up in one word: boring.
A blank mask appears at your feet, wearing a smile that is not quite a smile. You know that your Elation has been acknowledged, and it is time for you to reforge the rules of the World in Canvas.
The Phantasmoon still gazes quietly from the rim of the sky, as if to witness how you will use this power. The Phantasmoon is no different from the one that shone upon the ancients.
And so, yet another Phantasmoon Games of the World in Canvas begins...

You open your eyes. Sunlight glints off the glass facades of skyscrapers, while a stream of aerocars stretches into the sky like a long dragon. Time to go to work. You hop out of the billboard you call home, fishing a tie and a suit out of a briefcase that consists of nothing but line art.

As one of the first batch of imagenae salvaged by the Worlds Reborn Initiative, you witnessed these skyscrapers rising from the ground up. The IPC granted you human rights and invited you to join this tide of universalization. The cost? Well, even imagenae have to clock in for work.

"Your Wishpower balance is nearing the danger line." The digital watch scribbled in crayon on your wrist squawks. If you don't have enough Wishpower to sustain your body, you'll have to compete with the graffiti on the walls for work. By then, you won't be far from disappearing completely.
*Clang!* Something suddenly flies out of the trashcan and smacks you right in the back of the head. You spin around in anger, only to discover it's a blank mask...

The Phantasmoon gazes quietly from the edge of the sky, wearing a goofy grin. You understand that with this gift, you can rewrite your destiny however you please, and it all depends on where you want to lead it.
And so, the first Phantasmoon Games after the reconstruction begins...
You open your eyes to find yourself lying in a culture medium of the School of Pure Creation. Two people in IPC uniforms stand outside the glass tank, one looking a bit flashier than the other.

"Supervisor, I guarantee you, the 'Humorous Robot' is definitely humorous enough this time." The earnest researcher wipes the sweat from their brow with a handkerchief. "More humorous than me, at least."
"In that case, tell me a joke." The supervisor pats the control panel. "You can understand me, right?"
"What comes in thick and thin, makes people want to dance, and makes them cry? Answer: Electric wires."
"I have the best joke up my sleeve. I really want to tell it, but unfortunately, I don't have hands right now... let alone a sleeve."
"I have a friend who's a half-borisin. His dad is a borisin, his mom is a borisin... but one time he ran into the Yaoqing, and now he's missing his lower half."
"Of course I can. I'm not Louis Fleming." You shrug.

"Cut the power supply." The supervisor hurriedly barked orders at the researcher. "Yeah, melt this whole thing down and incinerate the scrap in the red giant star. Just don't let Louis Fleming find out."
You are a Galaxy Ranger, riding a comet as you roam the cosmos, leaving a multicolored trail in your wake.

The Eternal Sprint, a game hosted on the Twin-Sided Planet did manage to make you break a sweat, but only barely. After crossing the finish line and pressing your gun barrel to the throat of the Twin-Sided Monarch, you waved off the crowd's gratitude and charged headlong into the next battlefield.
"..." A giant Void Mosquito approaches silently. You raise your gun and blast it to smithereens. Where will you deliver justice next? You look out at the distant sea of stars, pondering...
You adjust your angle and fire your gun for propulsion, flying in your chosen direction.

The sun of Bodlan has fallen into an eternal "Hunger." It's a fact known to everyone on this planet. To prevent their home planet from being devoured, the Bodlanians built colossal mass drivers on the surface, feeding the star by launching matter into it.
And now, yet another feeding season is upon them. To satisfy the sun's greed, everyone must do their part, be it with supplies, lives, or... concepts.
And you, this quarter's head feeder, will decide what stays and what goes.

People tear out their consciences, dragging forth the benevolent and the righteous, and shove them all into the launch pods. The survivors laugh as they grovel, praising your brilliance. You have lost nothing, yet you have lost everything.
The sun sticks its tongue out, swallowing all the tributes whole. Beneath its blinding radiance, you are permitted to live on... until it grows hungry once more.

The excavators bellow, uprooting homes, land, and memories, dumping them all into the launch pods. The elderly embrace and weep, while the youth wipe away their sweat. The weight of homeland rests differently in everyone's hearts.
The sun sticks its tongue out, swallowing all the tributes whole. Beneath its blinding radiance, you are permitted to live on... until it grows hungry once more.
People pull out books, chips, and erudite minds, tossing them all into the launch pods. No protests, no crying, smart people know when to shush.
The sun sticks its tongue out, swallowing all the tributes whole. Beneath its blinding radiance, you are permitted to live on... until it grows hungry once more.
You're just another netizen in Duomension City. The web is your second home, and your account is your second body. After years of surfing the cyberworld, you've finally lost your mind.

Madness is a good thing, because it allows you to see the truth of the world clearly. Now, as you stare at a screen full of trash memetic content, a truth emerges before your eyes: "Only by grossing others out first can you avoid being grossed out yourself."
The total amount of Elation in the universe is constant, which means smiles don't disappear: They simply get passed on to you. That's what we call the Law of Conservation of Elation.

As a cake merchant, you make a living by crafting cakes through bizarre methods, having opened your own shop on the streets of Duomension City. Your cakes seem to see through people's deepest desires, and every day, customers line up from the street entrance all the way to the exit.

One day, a man dressed in black walks into the room and whips out an ID: "I'm a security officer from the Department of Aberration Defense. By order of the executive, I'm here to shut down your shop."

You recall the news from the other day about several Iwoz shapeshifters escaping the zoo. Rumor has it they can turn into any living creature. The security officer in front of you might be a shapeshifting fake, but he could also be the real deal.
Power is clearly more worthy of respect than the truth. You pay a large amount of Wishpower fine just to buy some peace. Before leaving, he even swipes a piece of cake from the windowsill.

You let out a roar and lunge forward to tear at the fake security officer's disguise, wrestling with him in a heap. Countless cameras capture the scene, spreading across the internet at the speed of a sprinting Furbo Journalist. Your likes are shooting up...

You pour every ounce of your being into crafting a cake of extraordinary artistic merit. Shapeshifters from miles around swarm in, and the crowd erupts in awe. Before long, the real security officers show up and sweep the lot of them off the streets.

Enough small talk. You look at the target's back. The fire of rage that has spread from your ancestors begins to burn. Only when he's dead will you finally be able to breathe. Every cell in your body bellows: REVENGE!

But besides your anger, revenge also requires cunning and patience. After months of casing the joint, you've nailed down your enemy's schedule. There are a few perfect spots along his route of action, and it all depends on where you choose to make your move—
Covered head to toe in paint, a carefully prepared disguise... You've turned yourself into a part of the mural, waiting around for the poor victim to pass by...

You wait and wait, until Phantasmoon falls asleep and the police dogs start their street patrols, but you still don't catch a glimpse of the figure that occupies your every thought. Tough luck, your nemesis didn't pass by here.
The curtain parts, and hot steam billows out. Amidst the clank and clatter of pots and pans, life-sustaining Wishpower is born. But you are here to end a life.

Your enemy cautiously takes a seat, clearing away the crowd. But you've already turned the food and cutlery in the restaurant against him. Tables and bowls flip, but only the food goes flying. The one who truly deserves to die is unharmed, bolting out the door with a piece of bread in his mouth.

You step into the lobby surrounded by wispae, push past the eagerly soliciting lightpaw, and head straight for that room. The club is strictly private, yet your steps are resolute, like an Aberration drawn by Wishpower.
The wispae scatter and flee. Your enemy's face is filled with confusion and shock... absolutely delicious. You close the door, and what happens next needs no elaboration...
Covered head to toe in paint, a carefully prepared disguise... You've turned yourself into a part of the mural, waiting around for the poor victim to pass by...

You wait and wait, until you finally see the figure occupying your every thought appear from around the corner. You embrace the enemy before you passionately, slipping the tip of your blade right where it belongs.
The curtain parts, and hot steam billows out. Amidst the clank and clatter of pots and pans, life-sustaining Wishpower is born. But you are here to end a life.

Your enemy cautiously takes a seat, clearing away the crowd. But you have already turned the restaurant's food and cutlery into your allies, and they launch a sudden, violent ambush, swallowing your foe whole.

You once had an enemy, but no longer. You stand amidst the wreckage, taking a deep breath of the sweet, metallic air. The corpse doesn't get back up. Looks like they weren't a Denizen of Abundance after all.

People say revenge leaves you with nothing but an endless void, but you disagree. Right now, you feel an unparalleled thrill. Every cell in your body is sparking with Elation. You absolutely must do something to celebrate!

Much like a classic villain taunting the detective, you boldly announce the culprit's identity to the security officers: yourself. Countless eyes, accompanied by a surge of converging Wishpower, fixate on you. This is bound to stir up trouble, but that just means a brand-new adventure.
You lean down and take what is rightfully yours from the enemy: be it from their pockets, their mind, or their still-warm fingertips...
What a rush! How exhilarating! You holler, you run, you tear your clothes to shreds. It feels as if you've become a skyfang, ready to swallow the Phantasmoon whole!

The adventure is nearing its end. Riding a massive ship, you and your companions crash through the raging waves and finally set foot on the legendary Jelly Island. The scent of love and courage fills the air.
"Hehehe, it's not over yet..." The wicked witch controls her golem, poking her head out from behind a soft mountain. Her candies possess a soul-captivating magic.
"Either hand over your sword or eat these candies! Otherwise, my Wabbie Waboo and I can't let you pass." She holds out a pumpkin basket full of candy, glowing with an eerie light.

Compared to your destination and your companions, treasure and power are nothing important. You hand over the sword that has been with you this entire journey, and the jellies watching from afar breathe a collective sigh of relief. The department head playing the witch smiles and takes your hands. This is the story of the Knights of Arcadia.
Even today, you often think back to that game from years ago. In your dreams, by the side of the road, in moments of déjà vu...

You wanted to refuse, but those candies simply looked too delicious, and they were. You all crowd around the department head playing the witch, who laughs and pats your heads. This is the story of the Knights of Arcadia.
Even today, you often think back to that game from years ago. In your dreams, by the side of the road, in moments of déjà vu...

Ever since the first amoeba looked up at the sky, exploring the cosmos has been the dream of every intelligent species. But Morguren's atmosphere is enveloped year-round by plasma storms, forming a deadly cocoon. For thousands of years, no spacecraft has ever managed to tear through that scorching canopy.

Looking at the nearly completed unmanned rocket, you and your team exchange high-fives in celebration. You only need to wait for the storm's off-season, and then you'll achieve the monumental feat of touching the cosmos... at least there's a chance you will.

"Sell it to me," a flamboyantly dressed wealthy merchant says. "Look at how vibrant the colors on its hull are. If we turn it into an amusement park, the kids will absolutely love it. Nobody can make it through the plasma storm anyway. It'd be a shame to just blow it up."
Silence spreads through the room like a thick fog, and everyone turns to look at you. Rationally speaking, the success rate for this launch is indeed almost zero.
"Wise choice," says the merchant while paying the bill with children's laughter. An amusement park was completed shortly after, and you never looked up at the sky again.

The rocket pierced through the lightning-filled sky like a pebble tossed into the ocean. Fire and the sound of an explosion follow quickly after... Your entire investment just went up in smoke, but the experience still remains.
"Next time. Next time it'll definitely work." You clenched your fists, telling yourself and your colleagues.

The Morguren atmosphere is perpetually shrouded in plasma storms, and no one has ever successfully touched the sky. You and your team could have achieved this feat, but fell short at the final hurdle.

That failure provided you with a valuable lesson. Numerous expert opinions were put forward, and numerous technical issues resolved. Today, the brand-new bright steel rocket once again stands tall astride the Earth, bringing with it a war that nobody remembers the reason for.

"For the sake of Ublatutuckpo, your rocket will be requisitioned as a missile. Quit stressing, you'll love it." The four antennae on the officer's head swayed, prompting your team to immediately grab their wrenches and straightedges.
Just say the word, and they would willingly defend this achievement with their lives, even if the cost was destined to be paid in blood.
The soldiers dismantled the research equipment, repacking bombs instead. You watched the rocket launch smoothly into the sky, turn, then unleash a tide of fire at the edge of the horizon...
"A perfect trajectory," marveled the officer. "This is your reward."

A battle broke out, and blood spilled across the ground. The fire of the launch trail illuminated the survivors' faces. You looked up, watching it rush into the storm, never to be seen again, just like the departed.
"We will remember this lesson," you muttered. People embraced and cried, then got up and continued their work.

Under the Morguren sky, a brand-new giant rocket stood tall once again, taller and more beautiful than ever before. Across the screen, the R&D team met your gaze, quietly awaiting the moment of launch.
Unhindered by destiny, with no wasted words, the rocket ignited and ascended into the sky. It pierced through the particle cloud shell, then popped its head out from the far side of the sky.
You did it. After dozens of Amber Eras and millennia of trying, the Morguren people have finally touched the stars. In this zero-gravity ocean, you feel as free as a newborn.
"Go, Captain. Set a course for our destination." The voice of the command center came through over the comms, and you tightened your grip on the controls...
The ship's engine lit up again. You drew an elegant arc and sailed into the deep space.

You have been stuck in the Mourning Cave for ages... You have become unkempt, with a weary look in your eyes. If anyone were to come and help you at this moment, you would see them as your salvation.

As you are contemplating whether to save yourself by making an eye-catching sign as bright as the *Beacon Coloring Paste*, you hear an ancient and beautiful song - The song, as refreshing as the clear rain, soothes your soul like a pot of honey tea.

"It's our honor to meet a soul as tenacious as yours. We are the Knights of Beauty, and we'll show you our passion through our spears." Along with the clanking sound of armor, a burst of dazzling light envelops you... You hear the sound of a descending massive airship. While drifting in and out of consciousness, you can only vaguely hear them discussing how to rescue you...

Yet... the discussion lasts for a very long time. They shower you with praises before introducing themselves. After analyzing your predicament, they provide you with dozens of targeted solutions... You find the situation more and more confusing, and you start to wonder whether they can be trusted.

lines: You stumble into a familiar place. You look up and find her standing before an experiment bench. Holding an embroidered cloth with her left hand, she pulls the thread on the last needle with her right hand before gently biting it off.
"You've barged into my world slice once again." Ruan Mei's voice is calm as she speaks with her back facing you. "I haven't finished cultivating my work yet."

She hesitates for a few seconds before turning around to look at you... After a moment of tense silence, she sighs and steps down from the bench. The mouthwatering scent of snacks permeates the air. "Since you're here, take a look at these patterns for me, and pick the one you think is the perfect masterpiece."
"If you answer it correctly... you'll be rewarded."

"Great choice. Don't sweat over it. There's no such thing as a perfect masterpiece in life. I was just testing the inclination of your heart." Ruan Mei returns to the bench. Her heels give off a crisp clacking sound when she walks. "Questions without a standard answer are created to search for the unattainable answers."
"Here's your reward."

"The more you deposit, the higher the interest rate!" A familiar voice arrives.
You show your empty pockets to the bank teller, and the smile on his face freezes! It's time you claim your promised rewards!

options.desc: You withdraw the sealed Cosmic Fragments together with interest.

lines: Despite having traversed the Simulated Universe for eight million miles, you did not find anyone who truly understood you...
You are tired of continuously testing one project after another. So, you decide to adopt a worm as your companion in the Simulated Universe.

You observe your companion: This beautiful space worm is named Sweet Saliva. It secretes secondary metabolites around its wound that give off a unique flowery, fruity, and sweet scent... You know that when it matures, it will linger around the exotic fruit orchards and cosmic tea plantations. Each of its trips may bring the scent of *love* to you.
Although you are destitute... you can still do your best to nurture it.

options.text: Feed the Erethian galaxy's "sea salt snack."
options.desc: Lose  Curio(s).

options.text: Use the specialty "cleaning foam" of Washtopia.
options.desc: Lose  Blessing(s).

options.text: Feed the Vortex Colony's "special milk tea."
options.desc: Lose  Cosmic Fragment(s).

lines: Your space worm wriggles and spurts a mouthful of saliva at your face to show its gratitude to you.
Oh... You feel so happy!
Your space worm is wriggling. You wait for it to spurt a mouthful of saliva at your face...
However, it leaps and smacks its tail against your face instead! It hurts a lot!
...Seems like it hates to be treated this way.

Time flies. The space worm named Sweet Saliva that you have nurtured has been undergoing immersive learning at the cosmic tea plantation for a long time... When you hear the sound of fumbling at the door, you know it is back.

You open the door and find that it has grown up. Its skin, which was initially green, has faded and is now covered by a colorful pattern that is a mixture of white, yellowish green, and brownish blue hues... They are the signs that Sweet Saliva has matured into an adult bug. It calls out for you... which is the proof of its *love* for you.
A relieved and sorrowful smile breaks out on your face.

options.desc: Obtain  random Curio(s).
Obtain  Blessing(s) of 3-star rarity.
You just want to keep giving... You don't expect anything in return at all.

lines: A person carrying a trashcan meets you. He crouches down and shows you his treasured trashcan.
"This is an incredulous space." He beckons. Then, he tosses out some collections of pitiful love poems from the trashcan to make some space for you.
In a hushed voice, he says, "Put your waste in it, and the items will evolve into an advanced awareness, then come running out energetically on their own!"

options.desc: Discard 1 Curio and obtain 2 random Curios.
You are not interested the trashcans.

lines: A foxian dancer approaches you. She makes a mischievous shushing gesture at you before lifting the curtain to the hall for you.

"Before these seven pots of incense kneel countless dancers from all over the stars, who are getting madder by the day. They prostrate themselves before the meeting hall, and sing and pray to the <unbreak>13</unbreak>th self-strangler - there are already <unbreak>13</unbreak> of them. The dancers will lie prone before God, pleading to know their end after the cosmic dance ends."
"Here's a talisman about your fate. If you don't believe this type of thing, just treat it as a famous rumor of the cosmos."
A talisman stained with blood from an unknown source is placed before you... You regard it contemptuously and remain completely unimpressed. In your opinion, there is no such thing as fate...
Deep down inside, you are tempted...

options.desc: Spend  Cosmic Fragment(s). There is currently a <unbreak>3[i]%</unbreak> chance to draw Destiny's Revelation.
Once you start it's hard to stop.

lines: You wipe the blood off the talisman on which it reads: "Consolation." You are very disappointed...
Ready for another one?

lines: This is unbelievable... Your hands are trembling, and tears are streaming down your face. Being an unlucky dog all your life, you never expected to experience something as *wonderful* as this. You even wonder if everything is still just a simulation...
Surprisingly, you have received a genuine revelation from fate. The talisman reads: "The Revelation of Finality..."
You pass out from excitement before you can finish reading it.
You come across a massive fragment of the Mirror of Transcendence. Three candles are placed beneath it as offerings.
You walk back and forth while being deep in your thoughts...

options.desc: You yearn to get a response from THEM.
You don't want to make a wish.

lines: As one of the candles is lit, a vague image of the God of Beauty's broad face flickered within the fragment... Just as the image gets clearer, the face of a Mirror Holder suddenly appears within the massive fragment!
"I've been imprisoned in this mirror fragment for a long time. Believe in the Beauty, and I will grant all your wishes," says the Mirror Holder in the mirror.

options.desc: Obtain random rewards.

options.text: Make a wish to get her out of the mirror.

You encounter a freckled man with curly chestnut hair who introduces himself as a digger in the Black Forest. He describes the forest as a mysterious place. It is said that in the forest there are numerous prophecy machines, poet machines, and all kinds of mechanical lifeforms operating on gears. Organic lifeforms rarely set foot there.
His face brightens up the moment he sees you, as though he has just found a potential fellow enthusiast. He places his treasure — a cuckoo clock — into your hands.
"Bring a cuckoo clock home and try using it!" The cuckoo clock fanatic says. "I'm sure you'll fall in love with cuckoo clocks."

options.desc: Obtain 1 random cuckoo clock series Negative Curio.
It doesn't feel right!

lines: He is thrilled, thinking that he has met someone who shares his taste!
He looks upset when you turn him down. He seems to be a very sensitive person, but that does not dampen his fervor!

"Please... Please take it... I've never succeeded in promoting the cuckoo clocks. Nobody could appreciate them. If no one could really appreciate the cuckoo clocks... then my life will be meaningless..." His eyes glisten with tears, and he is on the verge of crying.
He keeps pushing your shoulder as he persuades you to go home and study the cuckoo clock - Just take it back home and enjoy using it!

You run into the cuckoo clock fanatic with the curly chestnut hair again! He greets you enthusiastically when he sees you. You notice that he has just ended a phone conversation with a Black Forest digger...
"It's you again! We're going to establish the Cuckoo Clock Fan Club! Would you like to experience the charm of other cuckoo clocks?" His enthusiasm is at full power before you are even ready for it.

options.desc: Obtain 1 random cuckoo clock series Negative Curio and a 2-star Blessing.

options.text: Return the cuckoo clock to him.
options.desc: Discard all cuckoo clocks.

lines: You've received another cuckoo clock! If things go on at this rate, you might one day become a cuckoo clock fanatic yourself. That thought puts you in fear...
He is devastated. He cannot understand how someone can resist the temptation of a cuckoo clock...
He leaves with a sigh.

This time, you are mentally prepared for it. When you see the cuckoo clock fanatic with curly chestnut hair walking in your direction, you are convinced that nothing will make him give up. However, you are ready to face him!

"Oh, my old friend! It's been a long time! I've just bid farewell with all the inorganic beings in the Black Forest." The cuckoo clock fanatic starts sobbing when he sees you. "I've contacted the Business Development Department of the IPC, and they've promised to help us promote our fan club in the universe! We'll be a stronger team soon!"
There are a lot of newly excavated cuckoo clocks behind him...

options.desc: Obtain 1 random cuckoo clock series Negative Curio and a 3-star Blessing.

options.text: Exchange the cuckoo clocks you've gathered with him.
options.desc: Give all cuckoo clocks to your opponent in exchange for the same number of Curios.

lines: You can feel yourself succumbing helplessly and turning into a cuckoo clock fanatic...
He is over the moon! You finally comprehend the great work he spent his life setting into motion - The great work of making everyone understand the joy of ensembled tradeable cuckoo clocks!
