options.text: The divine are experts at torturing people.

lines: And so the long torture began. The young devotee, a fisherman's son, devoured all the fish and shrimp his father had caught.
Then, he consumed all the wheat in his home, and the provisions of his neighbors. To find more food, he was forced to leave his homeland. He devoured all the birds and beasts within his sight.
But as Cerces had foretold, no matter what he ate or how much he consumed, eternal hunger continued to torment him.

This painful journey continued for an unknown amount of time. Finally, the devotee exhausted his strength, his spirit and body utterly broken. He sat before a withered tree, sensing his imminent demise.
Using his last ounce of strength, he raised the seeds given by his god, and instead of putting them in his mouth, he scattered them into the air.

options.text: He wasted the last of the food.

lines: The seeds blossomed with Cerces's blessing in the air, and the withered tree behind the young man transformed into a towering Sacred Tree.
The young devotee had passed Cerces's test. Thus, various crops began to grow upon the earth, and people gathered beneath the Sacred Tree to listen to the teachings of the voice of wisdom.
When the phantom night of Oronyx still dominated the sky, in the boundless Evernight, a giant bird whose wings could cover the land opened its eyes.

Aquila sensed everything around them. They opened their first pair of eyes, but the dim world prevented them from seeing clearly. Then they opened their second pair of eyes, but darkness still enveloped everything.

So they opened more eyes, on their head and wings. With each pair of eyes Aquila opened, the world became a little clearer. Finally, when they opened the hundredth pair of eyes, Aquila could at last see the world they inhabited.
When Aquila saw the world clearly, the world was also within their eyes. From their eyes came a blazing and absolute light, outshining the Veil of Evernight and the stars embedded upon it.
The night was over, and the earth welcomed the first ray of sunlight since the birth of the world.
Aquila established their divine realm at the border of Amphoreus. The short feathers on their wings became the glow and flames in the sky. The long feathers were fashioned into thunder and lightning.

Clouds were Aquila's first Titankins. They took the white from their own eyes to create clouds. These kins forever float around their master, but they cherish freedom and are naturally carefree, thus easily indulging in pleasure.

Sometimes, the clouds would be tricked by Phagousa into drinking vintage wine, thus wetting Aquila's feathers. The angry Aquila would then shake their body, casting the wet feathers into the clouds and summoning thunderstorms.
But some poets claim this happened because Phagousa secretly encouraged the clouds to tickle Aquila's nose, causing them to constantly sneeze in the sky.

options.text: Their every movement affects the weather.
Phagousa is a wee bit naughty.

lines: When the children of humanity first descended to the world, they looked up, yet lost their sight to Aquila's piercing gaze.
And the divine light emanating from their eyes was so scorching that the earth melted into magma, and plants were charred black from the heat.
Aquila circled across the sky, hearing the countless pleas rising from below. Moved by a tinge of compassion, they slowly closed one pair of eyes.
At that moment, the wailing grew a little fainter. So Aquila closed another pair of eyes.
And so this continued until Aquila left only a pair of eyes open, the voices of the people turned to praises and cheers.

options.text: As they say, heed the needs of the people.

lines: And so, Aquila received their revelation — to create a new Titankin with only a single pair of eyes.
When the leader of Kadir encountered that towering, sun-like figure in his dream, he did not yet realize that he was about to be granted the wisdom to cross the ocean.
Long ago, in Phagousa's most unrestrained era, even the greatest coastal city-states could only pray not to attract their fickle favor.
Just as the leader of Kadir led his people to toil day and night, hauling stone and fortifying the dikes, all in the hope that their home would not be destroyed in one of the sea god's wild revels.
But the world is fickle, and fate seldom favors human effort. Instead, their toil only amused Phagousa, who, in their playful whim, raised towering waves and swept the dikes away.
The second time, the leader carved deep trenches along the shore, hoping to halt the advance of the waves. But Phagousa's power filled the ravines and surged onto the beach once more.

options.text: Humans are powerless against the gods.
But he is still a fighter.

lines: Twice defeated, the leader was consumed by sorrow and fury. He roared at the sea, condemning the injustice of this one-sided struggle.

Phagousa was not angered by his outburst. Taking the form of a great whale, they appeared by the shore and spoke to the people. If the people could cross the sea and reach a distant island within seven days, they would cease their disturbances and even bestow upon them Phagousa's treasures.
But if they failed, the coastline would be swallowed by the ocean forever. With that, the great whale vanished into the depths.
The leader pondered for five days and nights but could find no way to cross the sea. That night, in his dreams, he saw a figure as radiant as the sun — Aquila.
Aquila told him that by binding sturdy branches together with vines, they could cross the sea.

At dawn, the leader gathered his people and set to work, lashing branches into rafts. On the morning of the seventh day, under the watchful eyes of his people, the leader embarked on his journey across the sea.
At last, the leader reached the island. But Phagousa, realizing they had borrowed divine wisdom, declared that they would flood Kadir's land with seawater.
In this moment of crisis, Aquila appeared once more to intervene —
"If you must flood their land, do not use seawater. Use the honeyed brew that is your pride and honor instead!"

options.text: Sounds like Aquila is also a PR expert.

lines: Phagousa, pleased by the flattery and amused by the clever words, was instantly satisfied.
From that day on, the warriors of the coast mastered the art of fermenting drinks and, before setting sail, would offer their respects to the sky.
But when Aquila boasted to Oronyx of their perfect Kin, they were met with nothing but a dismissive scoff.
"Is there such a thing as perfection in this world? Your so-called flawless Kin is nothing special."
How could the proud ruler of the heavens tolerate such doubt?
Blinded by pride and the desire to prove themself, Aquila tore out one of their own pairs of eyes with their beak and cast those — along with their lightning spear — into Georios's spine.

options.text: Not even divinity is safe from pride.

lines: From the soil, a child swiftly emerged, with a mind that could think and limbs strong enough to bear the weight of the world. With each breath, their body grew larger, and their wisdom deepened.

Until, at last, the infant became a giant, greater than even Aquila. They sprouted hands to touch the sky and legs to stride across the earth. Their hair turned snow-white, dyed by the clouds, and their eyes became deep blue, painted by the skies.
Thus, the omniscient and omnipotent Kephale was born.

options.text: A god begets a new god.

lines: However, before Aquila could boast to Oronyx of their creation, their path was blocked by an enraged Talanton.

The omniscient, omnipotent creation had disrupted the balance of the world. As punishment, Aquila and Oronyx — who had encouraged this defiance of cosmic law — were each condemned to rule only half of the sky, never to cross into the other's domain.
Aquila was ordered to forge a great scale and entrust it to the newborn Kephale. It would be the scale's duty to divide dawn and dusk, ensuring the balance between day and night.
When dusk fell, the Sky Titan would be compelled to close their eyes and enter a momentary slumber — until dawn called them back to wakefulness once more.
Yet Talanton did not realize that, having been born from Aquila's eyes, Kephale's gaze was naturally attuned to the light of day.
And so, in the ages to come, when humankind was born, they too would inherit Kephale's nature — working beneath the sun and resting beneath the stars.

options.text: Nighttime allows people to recuperate and rest.

lines: Thus, though the struggle between day and night would never truly cease, by the year's end, their hours would always return to perfect balance.
Ancient songs passed down through generations tell of that distant past — the march of the giant Kephale.
It is said that the giant was born from the conflict of day and night, and though they accepted their burden without complaint, when they gazed upon the world, they found it desolate.
The vast expanse of heaven and earth lacked the vibrant pulse of existence. Kephale, omniscient, understood in an instant — the world was missing life.
And so, with great strides, the giant set forth, vowing to seek the footprints of life.
To search every corner of the world, the giant followed the coastline. Their massive feet sank into the wet sand, sending mud flying in all directions.
Mud that splashed into the sea became swimming fish. Mud that struck the land turned into roaming beasts. Mud flung into the sky, dried by the sun, transformed into soaring birds.
The creatures born of the mud splashed in the waves, cried out from the earth, and called to their creator. But the giant walked too fast to hear them, leaving them far behind.

Kephale never stopped. With each step, the scale on their back shifted, exchanging day for night and night for day. They never paused, as if the moment they did, they would lose sight of the perfect life they sought.

The giant walked for an unfathomable length of time. Wishing to grant them a moment's rest, the Three Fates sisters gently draped the veil of night over their eyes, tricking them into believing that night had truly fallen.

Kephale then set down the scales, lay upon Georios's spine, and drifted into a brief slumber. As they slept, a single strand of their hair fell onto a stone. But because the giant continued to ponder the essence of life even in dreams, that strand of hair took root and grew into a mighty tree.

The tree sprouted with astonishing speed, and from it, wisdom and reason were born. Wherever its branches reached, the land blossomed with countless flowers, and even the creatures formed from mud were touched by its essence, gaining a spark of spirit.

options.text: Will one get smarter if they touch it?

lines: When the giant Kephale awoke from their slumber, the world had changed beyond recognition. Living beings gathered around the Sacred Tree and their creator, offering thanks for the gift of life.
But the giant was bewildered, unaware that this flourishing world had sprung from their own unintentional act. Perhaps this was the one truth they could never fully comprehend.
Ancient songs passed down through generations tell of that distant past — the mission of the giant Kephale.
The creations of the gods filled Kephale with joy, and the world thrived with newfound vitality. Yet, despite this, the giant remained unsatisfied —
"These beings, for all their beauty, still lack our wisdom. In time, they will crumble into dust."
And so, Kephale pondered deeply. Until, in a single moment of revelation, they understood their true purpose —
"I shall make them in my image, that they may bear the spirit of all things."

options.text: Humanity shall bear the spirit of all things.
They only realized it now? Does that count as a blind spot?

lines: The giant sought out the ruler of the sky, speaking with humble words —
"Your gaze is piercing and shines upon all the world. I hope that my creations may receive your blessing, so they may walk freely beneath the light of day."
Aquila smiled and readily agreed. Yet the god of the starry night frowned, turning away in displeasure —
"Please, do not be angered. When the stars rise, my creations will need your protection, so they may rest in peace."
Hearing this, Oronyx reconsidered — and, at last, granted their blessing as well.
The giant bent down once more and awakened the earth. Their creations would take form from Georios's divine body.

Then, the giant sought out Cerces, asking them to pluck the fruit of wisdom and grant their creations the gifts of reason and thought. The god born of the Sacred Tree had no reason to refuse, and even brought forth the curious Mnestia.

The goddess of love then flew to the mud figures, brushing their wings over the creations' eyes and gently touching their chests — so that their eyes might perceive beauty and their hearts might speak the words of love.
Everything was prepared. Yet the giant had not yet given their own blessing. So Kephale cut open their own arm, and golden blood flowed forth. This divine ichor bestowed true life upon the creations.
Thus, the first children of humanity came into being.
Humanity, newly created, gathered at the feet of the giant Kephale and built a great city.
And this city, founded beneath the giant, would one day be known as the Holy City of Okhema.
Ancient songs passed down through generations speak of that distant past — Kephale's nemesis.

Life spread across the land, but in the end, all living things met their death. From death arose conflict, and from conflict, war. As unarmed mortals fell, their souls plunged into the River of Souls, and within the realm of Thanatos, sorrow and hatred festered and grew.

The bones of the dead, fused with the waters of the River of Souls, were shaped by grief into a colossal figure. Beneath the earth, they unearthed the lightning spear that Aquila had once cast down when creating the giant. Tempered in the waters of the River of Souls, the weapon was reforged into the Lance of Fury.
Thus was born Nikador, the Lance of Fury — the eternal enemy of the giant.

options.text: Life will never yield to wars.

lines: The slaughter of countless creations filled the giant with sorrow.
Seeking aid, they turned to the Sky Titan, pleading for the return of the lightning spear, so that the divine weapon would no longer aid in destruction. But Aquila was unmoved —
"That spear has been tainted by the filth of the River of Souls. I will not lay a hand upon such corruption, much less reclaim it."
With no other recourse, the giant then called upon the god of wisdom, Cerces, to seek counsel. As expected, Cerces devised a plan —
"Nikador wields a divine shield, a gift from Thanatos themself. Forged from the very essence of the underworld, it is strong enough to withstand even the fiercest lightning."
"If you can convince them to strike their own shield with the spear — one of them is bound to break."
Thus, the giant journeyed to the River of Souls to confront its sworn enemy. They spoke with carefully chosen words, goading Nikador into action.
Proud of their unmatched strength and divine weapons, Nikador listened with scorn. Gripping their spear in one hand and shield in the other, they summoned all their might and clashed them together.

A thunderous roar split the heavens. The earth trembled as if struck by divine wrath, quaking for what felt like an eternity before settling into silence. As the dust cleared, the spear remained unscathed, but the shield had shattered into countless fragments.
Some say these fragments were later minted into coins by Zagreus. Others whisper that they became the secret behind the indomitable shields of Castrum Kremnos.

options.text: The Lance of Fury is really something.

lines: Thus, the giant had finally stripped its foe of one deadly weapon — But that was all.
Their struggle would not end here. It would carry on, stretching into the days yet to come.
Let's tell a story. An ancient fable where the characters tread the line between truth and falsehood, and the narrator is wholly unreliable.

A long, long time ago, a capricious god planted a flower among the ruins and raised the moon to illuminate the once-barren land. Over the long years, life gradually revived, and stories began to bloom.

On this day, where flowers bloomed and ancient trees took root, eight guests of distinct appearances met unexpectedly. Posterity called them the Mourning Actors. Though of course, that is also for you, the listener, to decide.

options.text: Or it could be the Aeons THEMSELVES.

lines: The first to speak was a boy with a gentle countenance. He gazed coldly at the moon, looking as though he had long since lost the capacity for joy or sorrow.

"I heard a rumor from a troupe leader of questionable repute that the Aeon of Elation once shed a tear here. So, I traversed seas of flames and forgotten storms to arrive at this very spot, all in hopes of reproducing that weeping moment."
"But all we see is a moon with changing faces." The man draped in a wolf's skin laughed. "Are we supposed to tell it all our stories?"

options.text: Perhaps THEY really can hear you.
Might as well, since we're already here.

lines: And so, the eight Actors sat together beneath the moonlight, sharing stories with one another. Some heard, some witnessed, some fabricated.
And then, there would be one who moves THEM to tears, proving that even the Master of Elation possesses a heart capable of compassion.
"Let's start with me." The boy closed his eyes, as if recalling his sorrowful past.
"It is a well-known fact that the universe is teeming with traces of the Elation. Aha creates games and offers rewards: treasures, secrets, or... genuine miracles."

"Like the Eternal Sprint on Twin-Sided Planet, the Demon Lord Crusade on Vonwacq, the Card Game of the Future on the Pitch-Dark Star, and even a star that changes its trajectory after hearing a joke!"
The Actors chimed in, voices rising and falling, before swiftly piping down.
"In my homeland, tears shed during laughter crystallize into gemstones. So, the greater one's happiness, the wealthier they become."
"When there's too much to laugh at, the laughter stops, and the people grow poorer still. That is, until a young man on the verge of bankruptcy laughed at a beggar by the roadside."

options.text: Laugh at those weaker than you.
Laugh at those poorer than you.
Laugh at those more miserable than you.

lines: "Smiles require fuel, and there is always misfortune burning in the world to feed them. I repent for the laughter of that moment, and I grieve for my inability to find an ending where everyone embraces happiness."
"And so I came here, hoping to hear from Aha's own lips: does that world where everyone can smile truly exist?"
After listening to the boy's story, everyone fell silent for a long time. Then, a whistle broke the deadlock.
"Going by the order of our seats, it should be my turn now, right?" Under the man's wolf-skin hood were streaks of healed scars.
"Back where I'm from, we have a similar game... though perhaps 'ritual' would be a more fitting description." He feigned a casual air, yet his eyes were filled with melancholy.

"That winter, a troupe of Actors riding a pastry boat came to the village. Their bizarre otherworldly performances told heroic epics and comical stories, never repeating. Yet they also brought some uncertainty to the upcoming ritual."

options.text: I wanna go see the show too!

lines: "Don't sweat the details. Anyway, my best friend and I were armed to the teeth, and infiltrated the cave on behalf of the village to hunt a giant wolf, fantasizing about earning everyone's approval."
"The decennial hunt begins amidst the singing of a troupe from afar. Offer the vile beast's head to the deity, and the village shall know ten years of peace."
"In the darkness, I heard the wild beast howling. It tore at my arms, my shoulders... even when I fired a bullet straight into its eyes, it was all for naught."
"I nearly lost my mind back then. I cast aside my humanity, gnawing on that formless monstrosity... until the call of my best friend came to my ears."

options.text: Where was your friend just now?
You're still alive. That's enough to prove...

lines: "I ignited the torch. He, clad in wolf skin, was becoming one with the monster's corpse."

"In that moment, I saw the truth. The giant wolf had fallen hundreds of years ago. Its flesh was cast into the forest, its bones buried in the earth... yet its soul remained, its instinct still driven to slaughter."
"And so we donned the guise of the giant wolf, deceiving its soul with our own deaths, dissolving its desires. Life after life, generation after generation."
"I severed the monster's head and stripped its hide. People hailed me as a hero, yet never once asked about the other, who was already dead."

options.text: This story is just too fantastic.
An immortal monster is indeed terrifying.

lines: "Endlessly battling the immortal monster, even to the point of killing my best friend... tell me, what glory lies in such a wretched cycle?"

"I left my homeland aboard the troupe's ship. Years later, I reunited with the troupe master, and from her lips, I learned the story of Aha shedding a tear, which led me here, beneath this bright, unblemished moon."
The pink-haired girl lay by the tree, letting out a lazy yawn.
"What a coincidence. I saw that troupe master not too long ago. She was standing backstage, conducting a chorus of singers cut from cardboard."
"Sing of that ancient era, of the Imperator Insectorum's birth. Did the first Mourning Actors lend their Gondola to the Fools, or was it stolen by them?"
"Alas, I got distracted during that scene. All I remember is her boat made of desserts. Hey! It smelled sweeter than honey."

options.text: I know the rest of the story too.

lines: "Well, forget it." The girl licked her lips, mind clearly still lingering on the dessert. "The atmosphere here is way too heavy. How about I tell a fairy tale to lighten the mood?"
"In an era before the moon had risen, a serpent with a hundred heads coiled upon the earth. Its venom corroded the land, seeping along the horizon to permeate the starry sky."
"The Kingdom of Stars sent its most gallant knights, vowing to slay this wicked monster once and for all."
"The Lunar Knight severed its head with the crescent, the Wax Knight melted its body... The knights all played their part, finally severing the last immortal head."
"But none could have foreseen that the giant serpent's corpse refused to die. Its fangs pierced not only the knight's armor but also the moon itself."
"The wounded Lunar Knight was seized by madness from that day forth, his descent into frenzy fueled by the very moonlight."
"Doctors were summoned, but nobody knew what to do for the sick moon. That is, until a ship crafted from ice cream, donuts, and cake sailed straight into the moon."

"The show's laughter, drifting on the moonlight, drew in the sprites of mountain, water, earth, and sky. One after another, they leaped into the lake, passed through the mirror of its surface, and entered the very heart of the moon."
"The Lunar Knight reclines sideways upon the velvet curtain, letting out the occasional guffaw."

options.text: Is it that moon in the sky?

lines: "The troupe's performance lasted an entire day and night. Packed in among the sprites in the audience, I had succumbed to exhaustion well before the halfway mark."
"By the time I opened my eyes, the flowers on the ground had grown into towering giants, and the troupe had vanished without a trace."
"I stepped from the moon and found myself right beside you."
"Pfft... Thought she'd chicken out. Turns out I'm the late one." The girl blew her bubblegum, her petite frame radiating exasperation.

Her? It dawns on you that everyone here has a story about the silver-tongued troupe master, the odd soul who sailed in on a boat made of desserts. Before long, the room erupts with everyone sharing their first impressions of her.
"She claims to be a Mourning Actor, yet she loves to laugh more than anyone," "At the end of every show, she packs up her actors into her storybook"...
"She borrowed <unbreak>10,000</unbreak> credits from me. Or, to be precise, conned," stated the Intellitron lady.

options.text: Why is this thing different from the others?
Maybe she borrowed money from me, too...

lines: "Okay, my turn to go. I'll share how I met her. Think of it as a joke." With a casual wave, the girl conjured a series of vibrant game boards into the air.
"It all started with that box of Bathia Death Chess I scavenged from the depths of the trash. The ever-changing board was a metaphor for destiny itself, and I was utterly captivated."
"I bested every opponent, until I was left to play the game against myself. Piece by piece, I unraveled its laws, advancing toward the end goal I envisioned in my heart."
"Then I arrived at the answer: As Black, by adhering to a fixed sequence of moves, you are guaranteed to seize absolute victory on the <unbreak>101</unbreak>st move."

options.text: Guess that makes you invincible now?

lines: "With its solution narrowed to one, Bathia Death Chess became a rite praying to Aha for stability amidst the chaos."
"I became a puzzle-breaker, constantly cracking new games and conundrums. I can envision the finish line the moment I see a labyrinth, and foresee the outcome before the cards are even dealt."
"Admirers hail me as the optimal solution, yet I witness only the games I kill and a universe growing duller by the day."
"I was stumbling through a neon forest in a daze, drawn by the chime of the troupe's bells into a bizarre ice cream tent."

options.text: Kinda sounds like a horror story.

lines: "'Care for a game?' The lady's wicked smirk sent shivers down my spine. 'A game about the Aeons.'"
"'If you win, the RUBY_BGod of ElationGod of GamesRUBY_E will grant you an answer. But if you lose... wouldn't that just prove there are still plenty of things in life worth challenging?'"
"Before my departure, we played a single round of that most ancient of human games: rock, paper, scissors. The result... was a draw."
The Phantasmoon was still shy of its zenith, and the nightingale's trill spiraled with the stars. Just as the fifth actor was about to speak, a raindrop-patter of footsteps on gravel cut her short.
The woman was burdened by a vast pack, her dark clothes seamless against the dark night of Ahatopia. She declared herself a wanderer come home, yet admits she no longer knew the way.
Seeing that this encounter was itself a twist of fate, the group made room and gestured for the woman to join them, to share in the long vigil of the night.
"While you're here... and while the night is young, why not lend an ear to a traveler's tale? Consider it a change of pace." The woman gave a faint smile, one that carried an inexplicable warmth.

"I remember a homeland steeped in bitter dark, where people scurried about for survival, only to become the beasts' dinner, or to make dinner of the beasts. That was the world, turning like a great, grinding machine."
"My body etched with wounds, I savored the taste of my prey. The instinctive thrill of it... that was my first memory."
"Then, one day, a light of impossible beauty split the dark. I was drawn to it. I left behind the primal hunger, the old instincts... and I left my homeland."
"I came here. To the world of 'humans.'"
"Some hail me as a guest of honor, while others view me as a thorn in their side. This adoration and loathing make me lose my way."
"Here, I must scramble to meet their expectations, trade it for coins, and use those coins to purchase what was once free for the taking: a 'chance to survive.'"
"I feel fatigued and terrified. I want to flee, to return to the first, raw elation of my memory."
"But this world of happiness has stolen half my soul. When I look back, the path back has faded from my mind."

options.text: No one can go back there.

lines: "Yes. But still, I long to return to my homeland, to Mother's arms. I miss the moonless world, the warmth of the den, the sound of rain on leaves."
"I miss running the wild fields, the wind in my ears. I miss every night when the simple fact of being alive was enough."
"I miss the last beast I brought down, the taste of survival swallowed in my exhaustion, and the aftertaste that has never left me since."
"Me! My turn!" The fifth actor, utterly ignoring the mood, bounced like a living flame. Seriously, shouldn't she be a Masked Fool?
"At least for now, I'm playing a Mourning Actor." The young girl (questionable) replied.
"Hey, no passive aggression!"
"Anyway, we've got ages before my other selves track us down."

lines: "Ahem. So, the tale begins with Dr. Bloom being murdered by the Hanami Killer... Okay, actually, let's fast-forward a bit..."
"On the wondrous planet of Sparxraps, there was a mask called Hanami. Only the girl with the most fun can earn the right to wear it, becoming the center of attention and the heart of all laughter."
"Yet in time, Hanami always grows bored with its wearer. It then discards its current girl and drifts to the next performer it deems more entertaining."
"By hopping from one dull host to the next, Hanami became the undisputed girl of mirth and the planet's darling on planet Sparxraps."
"Driven by jealousy, a malevolent young girl takes on the mantle of Hanami Killer, seeking to destroy the mask and finish Hanami once and for all."
"But Hanami's acting was top-notch. She blended into the masses where no one could find her. The evil Hanami Killer took out Dr. Boom, Bunny Doll, and Little Flora, but none of them were Hanami."
"Then, one day, the Hanami Killer came for me. Plead as I might, and I was way too cute about it, she refused to believe I'd already been discarded by Hanami."
"We got into a huge fight, and I managed to slip away... I ran and ran, and ended up hiding in a troupe that came to Sparxraps to perform."
"And then it hit me... I had no answer. I don't know who I am, either."
"Perhaps Hanami never existed at all. It was only because people desired to play her role that she came to be."

"To evade pursuit, I was forced to forge a pact with the troupe master, taking on the role of a Mourning Actor and bound by our agreement... Hey, Boss! You're jumping the gun. I wasn't done with my line yet!"
Following the girl's gaze, a colossal ship made of desserts slowly sails out from the sea of stars, eclipsing the moon as it settles over Ahatopia.
Now, where were we? Let me think... Ah yes, in an age long past, eight Mourning Actors gathered in Ahatopia, each harboring the aspiration to move a God to tears through the power of story.
Just as the fifth Actor was rambling on, a colossal ship fashioned from pastries blotted out the night sky, and then—
"I walked all the way here from the sky. Ugh, I'm absolutely dead on my feet."
You can't shake the feeling that you've seen this lady somewhere before. That crimson color, like a pulsing font of boundless madness.

options.text: The Troupe Master drowning in debt.

lines: "What on earth are you after?" the hunter demanded, searching her eyes for an answer, yet finding only a bottomless chaos staring back.
The Actors need an explanation. Their gathering was no coincidence, but a carefully orchestrated encounter.

"But in the order of things, the one who should be telling the story right now... isn't me." The lady leaned forward, beckoning the silent young man into the lake, moonlight pooling softly across his shoulders.
Perhaps the moon truly held some magical energy of its own, whatever the case, the crowd's confusion was swept aside in an instant, all eyes turning toward the young man.
"Me?" He seemed caught off guard, but quickly composed himself. "Across the universe, countless great trees stand tall, reaching toward the sky."
"Legend has it that their fruit can heal all manner of ailments, even old age and death itself."
"Drawn upward by the lure of life, I climbed, gnawing on bark when hunger struck, drinking sap like wine when thirst took hold."
"After what felt like an eternity, I finally saw it, that tempting fruit above the clouds, wearing a face uncannily like my own."
"I swallowed it and pressed on. Up ahead, countless others had already clawed their way to the treetop, and behind them loomed an even taller tree."
"At the top of the tree hangs a fruit called 'Death.' Only by consuming it can one find release."

options.text: Talk about a matryoshka doll situation.

lines: "I kept climbing higher, shattered to pieces, then picked myself up and pushed on again, just like how they did it."
"Some unknown stretch of time later, I stared down at the clouds below my feet. An impulse seized me. And I leaped."
"I opened my eyes at the very beginning, picked up an axe, tuned out the noise around me, and swung it hard at the roots of the giant tree."

"I hew it down, yet it grows anew. But my life outlasts it all. When countless ages have passed and the sun itself is nearly extinguished, the giant tree will finally fall, and with it, the world meets destruction."
"They came to the ruins to mourn the silent Gondola, invited me to join them, and I gladly accepted, setting off on a journey to fell the next giant tree."

With that, the small girl gave the young man a pat on the shoulder, a small comfort, nothing more. The moon still hung in the eastern sky, stubbornly refusing to let its reflection sink into the heart of the lake.

"Hypothesis: Time here is not a trickle of sand through an hourglass," the seventh Actor began, her tone as cold as the metal shell that housed her. "What moves the moons is not the passage of time, but stories."
She dipped her fingertips into the lake, and the shimmering play of light and color rippled along with the motion.
"My story begins with a single teardrop."

"I was once a sculptor of renown across the cosmos. I carved shimmering palaces from seashells, shaped crystals into eyes, and even the ugliest clump of mud could transform into something beautiful through my hands."
"Yet 'sorrow' alone defies such gilded metaphors. A sculpture stripped of 'love or hatred' is nothing but cold stone."
"So I resolved to craft a single teardrop, a tear more melancholic than sorrow itself. If one could fully restore every facet of a single teardrop, perhaps true grief could be created."

options.text: How do you craft a teardrop?
How do you even define sorrow?
This was never going to work.

lines: "I passed by a church where oaths were being recited. A pious maiden bestowed upon me a golden crest, a token of gratitude for a moment's shelter."
"I walked across the wasteland of the eternal storm. The young man traveling with me broke off a branch bearing jeweled fruit, and offered it as a parting gift."
"I too have plummeted to the depths, broken and battered, only to be mended by an elderly couple. Before we parted ways, they pressed into my hands the most humble of screws."

"I set the gemstone into its core, cast its contours with gold, bound it in a shell of steel, and condensed a thousand treasures gathered along this journey into the most tender and precious of teardrops, and yet, my yearning remains unfulfilled. It still seems to lack that one crucial, final stroke."
"Just then, a gentle breeze swept across the table, coming to rest at the very edge of a teardrop."

options.text: Will this be the final stroke?
No one can replicate a single teardrop.
Like how no one can freeze a smile in place.

lines: "The breeze knocked over my work. It slipped right through my fingers and tumbled to the ground."
"A flowing warmth traced across my cheek, only to slip away in an instant, like every teardrop in this world, shattering the moment it falls."

"I set out on my journey once more, drifting from star to star, yet the perfect teardrop eluded me at every turn. Then one day, a Troupe Master sat with me by the seaside, and in casual conversation, began to speak of the Master of Elation's past."
"A moon, and a single teardrop."
"And this... is where my journey ends."
The Intellitron finished its account. By all rights, it should have been your turn next, but the first Actor suddenly raised a hand, the wings by their ears trembling in the evening wind.
"Um... has anyone else noticed? We aren't true beings, we're fictional characters in someone else's story. Everything happening here is nothing more than an ambiguous simulation."
Ahatopia fell silent. As if time itself had frozen in the wake of this staggering discovery.

options.text: Oh my, I can't believe it!

lines: "I noticed it from the very first line, but figured it'd just make things awkward if I said something." The hunter scratched his head.
"Wait, you didn't know!?" the pink-haired girl exclaimed, the realization hitting her a beat too late.
"Someone in this room holds the key to our questions." Guided by the words of the dark-clad traveler, all eyes turned once again to the Troupe Master, the grinning host of the banquet.
"Alright, alright, let's huddle up like the best of friends and listen to secrets from the past."
"In the age before the Hundred-Headed Serpent had perished, a band of fools stole Gondola and set off to slay the king of venality."
"In the shadow of the ship, the Knights from the Kingdom of Stars pulled off a grand deception. By sailing upon the true moon vessel, they advanced toward the Hundred-Headed Serpent."

"With the aid of the Train Knight and the Beeswax Knight, the Moon Knight finally severed the last head of the great serpent, but the Moon, dealt heavy damage by the monster, withdrew from all contact with the world and sank into the oceans of the sky."
"To reach the moon once more, the monkeys built a towering ladder, and the frog leaped with all its force, yet neither could reach it."
"But in a place where no one was watching, a lone frog swam against the current. It made its way to the pitch-black surface, paddling toward the moon's reflection shimmering in the water."

options.text: The moon cast its shadow up into the sky?
Or perhaps both are the real moon.

lines: "Who knows? After swimming for nine days and nine nights, it finally found the moon. There lay the crying of children, and the echo of laughter that were bound to be born after all weeping."
"The moon in the water was overjoyed for being found at last, but the frog refused its gift. What the frog wanted was not an offering, but a promise."
"Unlike monkeys who are perfectly happy on their own, the separated frogs need a leader."
"It weaves scattered tears into rain, guides lost actors onto stages, and strings countless tragedies into an epic show with an happy ending, leaving the audience awash in bittersweet wonder."
"And so, the moon embraced the frog's destiny, and thus set sail the first and only Troupe Master the Mourning Actors had ever known."
The moon rested with eyes gently closed, while beneath the curtain of night, the calls of monkeys, frogs, foxes, and rabbits rose and fell in turn, weaving into a lilting serenade.
But just then, a sudden burst of applause shattered the stillness of the night.

"By the story's timeline, I should not be here," said the one who applauded, their figure concealed beneath a flowing robe as they bowed to the audience all around. In the pale moonlight, you caught a glimpse of an ice-cold face. "And yet..."
"To be honest, I'm an Actor too, just like all of you. I'm here seeking an answer from the Master of Elation."
The man settled in beside you, hands folded over one another, their shadow falling across the water like a scene straight out of a play.
"Let's start with a gamble. There I was, sitting inside the belly of a monster, with hundreds of faces staring back at me from the stomach walls."
"Sorry, I forgot to mention something. So previously, since the death of the Hundred-Headed Serpent, the stars have circled each other tens of thousands of times."
"Yet the one hundred undying skulls refuse to rot, their howls ripping the ground. Moonlight spills into the goblet, and the rallying horn sounds once more."
"I knocked out the teeth of the largest head, but carelessly got swallowed into its gut."
"'Pitiful little monkey, let me think of how to torture you. How about we play a little game?' The monster cackled. But I said, 'Sure, but I get to decide how to play it.'"
"'If I can make your shadow disappear, you let me out of here. Deal?'"
"While the monster was busy gloating, I made my move and chucked the sun straight into its mouth."
"'Nom nom, delicious,' said the monster as it swallowed the sun whole. But a world without the sun is a world of pure void. And in the dark, there are simply no shadows to be found."

"'You have won,' the defeated one laughed with ten thousand mouths, 'but the serpent's venom has long since permeated this world. Among your comrades and successors, and upon that moon, a devil greater than I shall rise from your own ranks!'"
"I sought to prove it's wrong, to find a hero who could bring the moon to its phase of rebirth, and to snuff out the devil's cradle before it could grow up."

"Yet I have crossed vast seas of stars, and seen only sneering grins and sobbing tears erupt like a stench from the ruins, rotting moonlight and nebulae dissolving, blooming into the crimson fire of death."
"Then one day, by some twist of fate, I caught my own reflection in the water, and it all clicked. The devil had been here all along."
"A tragedy," the crowd murmured of the man's past.

"But that doesn't mean it can't become a comedy," the Troupe Master said with her usual smile, as if she had never shed a single tear. "You won a game, and as it happens, I have a story about a game."

"Legend has it that after being bitten by the great serpent, the Moon Knight slowly descended into madness. Miracles would grace those who bathed in its light, yet some were burned alive before ever breaking free from their cocoons."
"That night, I loaded the flower boat with comedies and tragedies, sweets and snacks, then quietly sailed it into the moon."
"'I know you, Troupe Master,' the Knight drew his sword and swung it at me as a gesture of welcome. Only to have it slice through a paper-folded curtain."
"It raised a glass to me. The venomous fangs that once bit the Knight had been ground to powder, fermented with moonlight into a fine brew. 'I will kill you, just as I killed that serpent.'"
"'But as the host of countless games, you cannot refuse my challenge.'"
"'Preposterous! You are nothing but my reflection in the water. Your strength, like you, will shatter at the slightest touch.'"
"'But who can say for certain, that the moon in the sky is not merely the reflection of the moon in the water, like a butterfly dreaming it has become human?'"

options.text: Which is real? Which is fake?
Is this some kind of scheme where one person plays two roles?
Or a disguise where two people share the same role?

lines: It doesn't matter. Just as light and shadow coexist, every coin has two sides. "The Moon Knight laughed so hard he nearly lost his breath, and granted me three games."
"'I have a goblet, if the moon can fill it to the brim, I shall offer up the past; I have a serpent's head, if a call can rouse it from slumber, I shall offer up the present.'"
"'I have one flower left. If a sword can cut it short, I shall offer up the future.'"

"The Knight poured moonlight into the goblet, but it slipped through the glass in an instant; he shouted the great serpent's name in fury, yet the remains lay drunk on the moonlight that dripped away."
"It swung its treasured blade at the bud, yet the flower swallowed the serpent bone's drunken dream and bloomed once more."
"I carried away a cup of the most pristine moonlight from the moon's palace, enough to illuminate the long night in a fleeting aftertaste."

"After hearing countless stories, the Moon Knight finally fell into a deep slumber, like the immortal serpent, burying its madness within dreams. Before closing its eyes, it made one last request of me..."
"Tell me another story. An ancient fable where the characters blur the line between reality and fiction, and the narrator is not to be trusted."
"So, that's why we're here," the first Actor said, barely concealing a smile. "To recreate the original Phantasmoon Games."
Eight Actors beneath the moon, each telling their own legend. Together, they forge a greater story.
**When the serpent stirs once more and madness claims all creation, eight Actors gathered beneath the moon will save the Kingdom of Stars in the far future together. That kind of story.**
"But come to think of it, isn't there still one person who hasn't told FherMhis story? I'm sure you know exactly who FsheMhe is." The lively girl said, flashing her signature mischievous grin.
You're about to speak when the silent man cuts you off. "Don't let this girl play you for a fool. You don't belong with us, and you're not one of the eight Actors either."

"We stand in the past, while you stand in the future, and so your story must be saved for a better tomorrow." The hunter removed his Actor mask and tossed it into the lake. "Give my regards to its master a thousand years from now."

"What if I secretly hid my own mask away. What would happen then? Would the future end up with seven Supplicants?" The short girl's gaze sank along with the mask, coming to rest in the embrace of the moon in the water.
"Forgot already? We're all just characters in a story. History's set in stone," the lady in black chimed in with a well-timed quip.

options.text: None of you are truly from the stories, are you?

lines: "Word has it the universe's first Fool and first Actor are one and the same. Long story short, our boss is a walking disaster. Please stop her from making any investments" A cold, mechanical warning from the Intellitron.
"Hey! Is now really the time for this?" Watching the Troupe Master fume, you can't help but burst out laughing.
"I can only hope you'll walk a path far different from mine," the devil sneered. "Become a hero, and then..."
"Let the moon shine as pure as it once did," the fox murmured, lost to sleep at some unknown point, its words spilling out as weird dream-babble.
Those of the past send forth their blessing to the future, and you are about to wake on the morning of the thousand-and-first night, like the moon in the water dreaming of the moon in the sky.

options.text: I still have one more question.

lines: What could ever move a god to tears? Does the Master of Elation harbor compassion within that jubilant heart?

"The answer has been staring you in the face all along. It's so easy, no one would ever believe it." The Troupe Master leaned in close, close enough for you to catch a glimpse of those star-like eyes of hers.
There, a single tear, one that has laughed with humanity and wept for them, without pause, since the very moment of its birth.
It is the moon, the forgotten past of Ahatopia, and the laughter that must inevitably erupt after a child's long, inconsolable tears.
